summary.overview: A gently luminous, pedal-anchored meditation in F major built almost entirely on one gesture: an F bass held underneath upper structures that drift among F6add9/Fmaj9, Bbmaj9(#11)/F, C11/F (heard as Bb/C over F) and Dm7/Dm9. Suspended sonorities make up 19% of the held duration and slash-over-F chords dominate every section, so the music hovers rather than progresses. It is classic Barnoski language: tonic pedal, stacked 9ths, 11ths and 13ths, plagal colour, and suspension favoured over resolution. The emotional core is warm, contemplative calm. It swells through a dark, low-register middle to a bittersweet peak on Dm9 at 2:11, then dissolves into bare sus4 and Bb/F shapes that never fully land.
summary.key_center: F major, with high certainty. Krumhansl gives F major at clarity 1, every local section estimate is F major, and an F pedal sits under most of the chord timeline (C13sus4/F, A#maj9#11/F, Dm7#5/F, Gm9/F). The runner-up, Bb major, reflects the heavy IV colour: Bbmaj9/D, Bbmaj7 and Bbsus2 recur constantly, and the piece ends on A#5/F (Bb over F, 2:52, 4.5 s), a plagal hover rather than a tonic arrival. Brief tonicization pulls come from three places. Section 3 leans on Dm11/C (1:34–1:37) over a C bass. D/C (D7 in third inversion, 1:55) acts as a secondary dominant that slides into Am7add11/Dm11/A at 1:56 instead of resolving to Gm. A fleeting Ebmaj13 (D#maj13 at 0:23, 0:34; D#M13#11 at 1:46) gives a borrowed bVII, Mixolydian/Aeolian tint. It is too short to register in the modal-colour detector, but it recurs and is probably real.

mood.overall: A warm, quietly radiant contemplation that deepens into a sonorous, bittersweet swell and then dissolves into suspended stillness.

dynamics_arc.description: A long, patient arch. Intensity rises almost monotonically from 0.43 at 0:00 to about 0.79 at 1:00 as the register descends and the voicings fill out. It plateaus near 0.71–0.80 through Section 2's heavy low chords (1:01–1:23) and dips slightly to 0.67 around 1:50 during Section 3's reflection. A second wave then climbs to the peak at 2:10–2:15 (0.85). From 2:20 the piece recedes steeply: 0.62 at 2:30, 0.42 at 2:45, 0.18 at 2:55. Across the whole piece the dynamic range is 36.1 dB, with the most dramatic contrast in the final 40 seconds.
dynamics_arc.climax_description: The climax at 2:11 is prepared by a 15-second ascent over an unbroken F pedal: Fmaj7/Fmaj9 (1:58) → C11/F → Bbmaj13#11/F → Gm9/F → C13sus4/F (2:01–2:05) → Dm7#5/F → Dm9#5/F → Bbmaj9#11/F (2:07–2:08) → Fmaj7 (2:09, 1.5 s). The peak lands on a 2.5 s Dm9, the relative minor with its added 9th, extended by Dmadd9 and Bbmaj9#11. The high point is a warm, aching minor-ninth sonority rather than a bright tonic arrival. Release comes through Fmaj7 at 2:17.

summary.texture_and_register: The piece is essentially pedal-point chord-melody. One hand (or the lowest voice) sustains F, or occasionally D or C, while the upper structures shift among 9th, 11th and 13th voicings. Register is used as the main structural tool. The opening sits high (median A4, about 672 Hz brightness), Section 1 drops an octave (A#3), and Section 2 plunges to D3 with the darkest timbre (423 Hz) and sparsest attacks. Sections 3–4 settle in the low-middle (C4 → F3) at the greatest density (38–40 notes/s). The outro spreads widest (A#1–D6) but thinnest, with bare fifths and sus chords left to decay. The overall span is D2–C6 with a median of G3: a warm, mid-low centre of gravity framed by glassy treble edges.
summary.emotional_narrative: 0:00–0:25: the piece begins as a glint in the treble, F-pedal sus chords and Bbmaj9#11 colours presented lightly, like a world seen through frost. 0:25–1:01: dropping an octave and gaining about 10 dB, the same F6–Dm9/F–Bbmaj9/F loop becomes a warm shelter, cadencing repeatedly onto F6 and Fmaj9. 1:01–1:23: the music descends into its depths, with heavy Bbmaj9/D and rocking F5/Fsus2 open fifths in the low register; it is loud but sparse, more solemn than climactic. 1:23–1:56: it lifts back to the middle and turns reflective, shifting the pedal to C under Dm11 (1:34) and passing through the borrowed Ebmaj13#11 (1:46), before the D7/C at 1:55 creates the piece's clearest forward pull. 1:56–2:20: a deceptive turn to Am/Dm11 launches the final ascent over the F pedal, reaching the bittersweet summit on a 2.5 s Dm9 at 2:11 and easing home to Fmaj7. 2:20–2:58: everything thins to Fsus4, Bbsus2 and bare fifths, intensity falling to near silence. The last word is an unresolved Bb/F hovering over the pedal: an ending that drifts away rather than closes.

imagery_cues.light: Cool, diffuse high light at the start, warming to amber as the register drops. It dims to overcast slate in the low middle, breaks into a brief low golden glow at the 2:11 climax, then fades to violet dusk.
imagery_cues.motion: Slow, continuous drifting with no hard cuts, matching the 85 BPM elastic pulse and low pulse clarity: gentle floating descent, lateral glides and slow push-ins. Motion broadens and slows in Section 2, gathers a gentle forward glide toward 2:11, and nearly freezes during the final 4–5 s held chords.
imagery_cues.scale: Intimate at the start (close-up crystalline detail), widening to human-scale warmth in Section 1 and vast landscape in the low-register Section 2. It stays expansive through the climax, then contracts back to intimate stillness and emptiness in the outro.

chord_vocabulary: C11/F = Bb/C over F (Fsus pedal sound, aka C13sus4/F)
Bbmaj9 / Bbmaj9#11 over F or D (IV)
summary.harmonic_highlights: Tonic pedal throughout: most chords are slashed over F (C13sus4/F, A#maj9#11/F, Gm9/F, Dm7#5/F), so I, ii, IV, V and vi all sound over one held F. The defining cadence, C11/F or C13sus4/F → F6/F6add9 (0:08–0:10, 0:26–0:38, 1:25–1:29, 2:01), is really a suspended IV/V-over-I resolving to tonic: suspension over resolution. Pedal shifts to D (C13sus4/D, C11/D at 0:31–0:34) and to C (Dm11/C, 1:34–1:37) briefly destabilise the floor. The borrowed Ebmaj13 (bVII) colours 0:23, 0:34 and 1:46 (D#M13#11); it is brief but recurring. Bbmaj9/D held 2.5 s at 1:03 opens the darkest section with IV in first inversion. 1:09–1:16 is a pure open-fifth meditation, F5 ↔ Fsus2 ↔ Fsus4. D/C (D7/C) at 1:55 is a secondary dominant that resolves deceptively to Am7add11/Dm11/A at 1:56. The climax at 2:11 lands on Dm9 (2.5 s), the relative minor rather than the tonic. The ending is plagal and open: Fsus4 ↔ A#5/F, with Bb/F held 4.5 s from 2:52, so the piece never returns to a plain F triad. Labels such as Emb6b9/C, Amb6b9/A# and Dm7#5/F are transcription aliases of C(sus), Bbmaj7 and Bb(add9)/F respectively.
summary.rhythm_and_feel: The tactus is 84.8 BPM with a strong underlying eighth-note subdivision (169.7). Steadiness is high (0.89) but pulse clarity is low (0.32): the beat is internally steady but softened by elastic rubato and long sustain pedal, so downbeats are felt rather than heard. Harmonic rhythm is fast on the surface, with upper structures changing every half-beat to beat (about 2 chord labels per second). The bass rhythm is extremely slow because of the pedals, which creates a 'busy surface, still floor' feel. Section 2 broadens markedly (2.32 attacks/s, 2.5 s holds). The outro relaxes to about 81.8 BPM with holds of 4.5–5 s, so the pulse dissolves into free time. Expect phrase-end lingering at cadences (e.g. F6 at 0:47, Fmaj7 at 2:09) and slight pushing into the climax at 2:05–2:11.
summary.relearning_tips: 1. Start with the core loop that generates most of the piece. Hold F2+F3 (or F2+C3) in the left hand. Cycle the right hand through F6add9 (A-C-D-G), Bbmaj9/F (A-C-D-Bb, or Bb-D-F-A-C), C11/F as a Bb triad over C (Bb-D-F over C), and Dm9/F (A-C-E over D-F), returning to F6. Practise it slowly at 85 BPM with eighth-note subdivision until it sits under your hands. 2. Learn Sections 1 and 4 next, since they share this material. Mark the 1.5 s Dm7 at 0:41, the cadence C7sus4/A# → Gm7add11 → C11/F → Fmaj9 (0:52–1:00), and the climax approach Fmaj7 (2:09) → Dm9 (2:11, voice it wide: D2-A2-E3-F3-C4). 3. Section 2: rehearse the low Bbmaj9/D (D2 bass, Bb-D-F-A-C above) and the F5-Fsus2-Fsus4 rocking (1:09–1:16) as a voice-leading exercise where only the G and Bb move above the fifth. 4. Section 3: isolate the pedal move to C (Dm11/C, 1:34–1:37), the Ebmaj13#11 colour (1:46), and D/C → Am7add11 (1:55–1:56). 5. Intro: transpose the core loop up an octave and arpeggiate lightly. 6. Outro: practise holding the sus shapes (Fsus4, Bbsus2, FM7sus4 = F-Bb-C-E) with control at pp. Let the final Bb/F ring the full 4.5 s without resolving. Throughout, treat transcribed oddities (Amb6b9/A#, Emb6b9/C, Dm7#5/F) as Bbmaj7, C(sus) and Bb(add9)/F.

sections.name: High Shimmer
sections.description: The piece opens in the treble (median A4, up to F6) with F, C/A and FM/C arpeggiated figures. Within four seconds it settles onto the governing sound, C13sus4/F at 0:04: an F pedal under Bb/C. Gm9/F (0:05) and A#maj9#11/C (0:07) follow, with Emb6b9/C at 0:06 likely an overtone-blurred C(sus) chord. 0:08–0:11 traces the home cadence C13sus4/F → F6 → F6add9 → Fmaj13. Dmadd9/F and Dm/F (0:11–0:17) dip into vi colour, then Bbsus2 and Bbmaj7 (Amb6b9/A#, 0:19) hold. A suspended turnaround runs FM7sus4/C → C7sus4/A# → C7no5 → the first borrowed Ebmaj13 (0:23) → Bb/F (Dm7#5/F) → F6 at 0:24, closing the phrase on tonic.
sections.character: Glassy and weightless, like the music is introducing its colours one by one without committing to a direction.
sections.dynamics: Soft (−29.2 dBFS), intensity rising steadily from 0.43 to about 0.6 by 0:25
sections.texture: Arpeggiated upper-register chord figures over a lightly sounded F pedal; moderately busy (3.88 attacks/s) but transparent
sections.register: High-middle to high: bass around A#2–F3, melody and voicings centred near A4, touching F6
sections.emotional_beat: Invitation: the tonal home and its suspended palette are laid out in light, hovering colours.
sections.imagery: Fine frost crystals catching pale morning light on a windowpane, each facet glinting in turn.
sections.label: High Shimmer (0:00-0:25)

sections.name: Settling Into Warmth
sections.description: The register drops a full octave (median A#3) and loudness jumps about 10 dB, so the same harmonic cycle now sounds rooted and warm. 0:25–0:32 alternates Bb/F and C11/F / C13sus4/F, then shifts the pedal to D (C13sus4/D, C11/D at 0:31–0:34), briefly undermining the F with a vi bass. Ebmaj13 colours the passage again at 0:34. The phrase resolves through Fsus4 → FM → Fmaj7 (0:35–0:36). The second half is the clearest statement of the piece's core loop: F6 / Dm9/F / Bbmaj9/F, a 1.5 s Dm7 at 0:41, then F6add9 and a 1.5 s F6 at 0:47. A C7sus4/A# → Gm7add11 → C11/F → Fsus24 cadence (0:52–0:55) lands on Fmaj9 at 1:00.
sections.character: Comforting and grounded, with the melody now singing in the middle of the keyboard and the harmony circling home repeatedly.
sections.dynamics: mp rising to mf: intensity climbs from 0.61 to 0.79 at 1:00
sections.texture: Fuller left-hand pedal with mid-register chord voicings and an inner melodic line; 3.33 attacks/s
sections.register: Middle: bass on F2/F3 and D3, voicings around A#3–A4, top near A5
sections.emotional_beat: Arrival and embrace: the hovering idea becomes a place to stand.
sections.imagery: Snowfall seen from inside a lamplit room, flakes drifting past a warm amber window.
sections.label: Settling Into Warmth (0:25-1:01)

sections.name: Deep Open Fifths
sections.description: This is the loudest section (−13.6 dBFS) yet the darkest and sparsest: the median drops to D3, brightness falls to 423 Hz and attacks thin to 2.32/s. It opens with a 2.5 s Bbmaj9/D at 1:03, IV in first inversion, with the D bass giving weight. G/F and C11/F follow. From 1:09 to 1:16 the harmony strips down to rocking F5 – Fsus2 – Fsus4 – FMadd9 shapes: open fifths with only the 2nd and 4th moving above them, a pure pedal meditation in the low register. Bb colour returns at 1:17–1:22 (Amb6b9/A# = Bbmaj7, held 1.5 s at 1:20; A#M), ending on C/A# at 1:22, a dominant-over-IV hinge.
sections.character: Sonorous and elemental, with broad chords ringing in the bass so the piece sounds deep rather than urgent.
sections.dynamics: f, sustained plateau: intensity holds about 0.71–0.80
sections.texture: Sparse, heavy low-register chords and open fifths left to ring; long sustains, few attacks
sections.register: Low: bass reaching D2, median D3, nothing above A#4
sections.emotional_beat: Descent into depth: the warmth turns inward and weighty, and the ground itself resonates.
sections.imagery: A vast snow-covered valley under heavy slate cloud, with the low hum of wind across open land.
sections.label: Deep Open Fifths (1:01-1:23)

sections.name: Circling Reflection
sections.description: The register lifts back to a median of C4 and the texture busies again (3.15 attacks/s, the most transcribed notes so far). It restates the home cadence C11/F → F6add9 → Fmaj7 → F6 (1:23–1:29), with a 1.5 s Dm7 at 1:29. 1:34–1:37 is a distinctive pedal shift: Dm11/C and Dm7add11/C alternate over a C bass, then C11 resolves to C11/F and Fsus24 at 1:38. 1:40–1:48 is the most colourful stretch: Bbmaj13 and Bbmaj7, A#M13#11 at 1:42, and the borrowed Ebmaj13#11 at 1:46. A Gm9/F → C13sus4/F → Fmaj13 → D11 turn (1:50–1:52) leads to Bb6add9 and finally D/C (D7/C) at 1:55, a secondary-dominant tension that propels the next section.
sections.character: Reflective and searching, as harmonic colours deepen and the music questions its home before pushing forward.
sections.dynamics: mf, easing from about 0.80 to 0.67 at 1:50, then re-tightening toward 1:55
sections.texture: Mid-register flowing chord-melody with inner-voice motion over shifting pedals (F, then C, then F)
sections.register: Middle: bass from D#2, median C4, top near A#5
sections.emotional_beat: Rumination: the familiar loop is reconsidered with richer, slightly unsettled colours, building toward a decision.
sections.imagery: Drifting snow eddying in slow spirals across a frozen lake under soft, shifting cloud.
sections.label: Circling Reflection (1:23-1:56)

sections.name: Bittersweet Summit
sections.description: D/C resolves deceptively to Am7add11 / Dm11/A (1:56), then the music re-anchors firmly on F: F6add9, FM9sus4, Fmaj7, Fmaj9 (1:57–2:01). The loop climbs through C11/F → A#M13#11/F → Bbmaj9/F → Gm9/F → C13sus4/F (2:01–2:05). It then intensifies over the F pedal via Dm7#5/F, Dm9#5/F and Bbmaj9#11/F to a 1.5 s Fmaj7 at 2:09. The dynamic peak at 2:11 lands on the longest-held chord of the section, Dm9 (2.5 s): the climax is the relative minor, not the tonic. Dmadd9 and Bbmaj9#11 (2:13–2:14) extend it, a cluster of E/A/A# colours passes, and Fmaj7 (1.5 s, 2:17) closes the arc.
sections.character: Full-hearted and bittersweet: it reaches its emotional height by leaning into minor warmth rather than triumphant major.
sections.dynamics: f building to peak (intensity 0.85 at 2:10–2:15), easing to 0.78 by 2:20
sections.texture: Densest passage (39.5 notes/s): rich full-handed voicings over a strong F pedal with an active inner line
sections.register: Low-middle core (median F3), bass to D2, top voices to A5
sections.emotional_beat: Climax and release: the long ascent arrives at a moment of tender, aching fullness on Dm9, then settles home on Fmaj7.
sections.imagery: A break in the clouds where low golden light floods a snowfield, every surface briefly glowing.
sections.label: Bittersweet Summit (1:56-2:20)

sections.name: Suspended Farewell
sections.description: The texture collapses to the quietest material (−33.1 dBFS): a 5 s Fsus4 at 2:20, then Bb/F (Dm7#5/F, 1.5 s) and a 2 s Bbsus2 (2:27). The outro is 44% suspended. FM7sus4 recurs (2:30–2:37) between Bbmaj7 and F5 colours, with a brief Fmaj9 at 2:36 and Fmaj7 at 2:41 as the last full major-7th sounds. From 2:45 everything strips to bare shapes: F5 → Fsus4 → A#5/F → F5 → Fsus4, rocking between tonic and IV over the pedal. The final chord, A#5/F (Bb over F, held 4.5 s from 2:52), never returns to a plain F triad, so the piece ends on suspension.
sections.character: Fading and open-ended, as if the music dissolves into air instead of closing a door.
sections.dynamics: p receding to ppp: intensity 0.70 at 2:25, falling to 0.42 at 2:45 and the quietest point (0.18) at 2:53–2:55
sections.texture: Very sparse long-held open chords (fifths, sus4, sus2) with wide spacing and long decays
sections.register: Widest span: bass down to A#1, median F3, isolated tones up to D6
sections.emotional_beat: Letting go: the warmth recedes to bare intervals and the question is left hanging in the air.
sections.imagery: The last few flakes settling on still, untouched snow at dusk, the air going utterly quiet.
sections.label: Suspended Farewell (2:20-2:58)

tempo.description: The measured tactus is 84.8 BPM, with a double-time eighth level at 169.7 and local tempos of 81.8–86.3. It feels moderate and unhurried, more 'flowing' than 'walking'. The attack rate of 3.25/s is only a little over two attacks per beat, and the harmony mostly changes every half-beat to beat while the bass barely moves. Pulse clarity is low (0.32) but steadiness is high (0.89): there is a steady inner clock, played with elastic rubato that blurs the downbeats. The time feels suspended rather than driven. Section 2 thins to 2.32 attacks/s with longer held chords (Bbmaj9/D for 2.5 s at 1:03), so it feels broader despite being loudest. The outro relaxes to 81.8 BPM with 4.5–5 s holds, so time nearly stops.

mode_balance.evidence: Major-dominant. Chord-quality shares are major 39%, minor 22%, dominant 10%, suspended 19% and dim/aug 1%, giving a minor-weight of 0.13. Most of the 'minor' share is diatonic vi and ii colour: Dm7, Dm9, Dm11/C, Gm9/F and Gm7. Much of it is also transcription aliasing of major chords. Dm7#5/F spells D-F-Bb-C, which is really Bb(add9) over F. Amb6b9/A# is almost certainly Bbmaj7, with the A as the major 7th. So the effective major weight is higher than the raw numbers show. Suspension is the defining modal ambiguity. C13sus4/F and C11/F both read as Bb/C over an F pedal, which blurs I, IV and V into one hovering Fsus sound. The outro is 44% suspended, so the piece's modality is 'major softened by suspension'. The only borrowed colour is the brief Ebmaj13 (bVII) at 0:23, 0:34 and 1:46. Bbmaj9#11 sounds Lydian but is purely diatonic IV with E natural, not a mode shift.

summary.overview: A slow, free-time meditation anchored almost entirely on an F# pedal, in which F# major is coloured rather than contradicted: the leading tone E# rubs against the root (transcribed as 'F/F#' and 'Fmb6b9/F#'), and add9, maj9 and sus2 voicings keep the tonic suspended instead of plainly resolved. The harmonic language is classic Barnoski. The tonic is held like a horizon, dominant colour floats above it (C#11/F#, C#13sus4/F#), and the subdominant Bmaj7/Bmaj9 opens the space. The relative minor D#m appears only at the peak and in the coda. Its emotional core is warm, grateful stillness that swells into a broad, slightly bittersweet climax around 2:23. It then dissolves into a quiet ending on an unresolved first-inversion tonic (F#/A#).
summary.key_center: F# major, with high confidence: the Krumhansl key is F# major, every section's local key estimate is F# major, and the most-held chords throughout are F#, F#maj7, F#maj9 and F#add9. D# minor, the relative minor, is the runner-up and is the main secondary colour. D#m is held for 3.5 s at 2:07, and D#m / D#m7 / D#m7add11 recur across 3:15–3:48. There are no true modulations. Instead the piece tonicizes or lingers on B (IV) at 1:16–1:22, 1:45–1:52, 2:53–3:00 and 3:29–3:35. It also leans on C# (V) as a dominant pedal at 2:27–2:32 and as a held half-cadence at 3:10–3:13. Much of the piece sits over pedal points: F# pedal in Sections 0–2, C# pedal at 2:27–2:30, and D# bass at 3:15–3:20.

mood.overall: A warm, grateful major-key reverie that swells to a broad, faintly bittersweet peak and then lets go into quiet, unresolved stillness.

dynamics_arc.description: The dynamic shape is a broad arch with a long plateau. From a quiet, low opening (0.31 at 0:00) the intensity climbs steadily through Section 1 (0.5–0.68) and Section 2 (0.67–0.76). There is a brief dip at 2:00 during the 6.5 s F# hold, then a surge to the peak at 2:10–2:30 (0.82–0.87). The music recedes to about 0.58 by 2:45, mounts a smaller second wave through Section 4 into 3:15–3:25 (0.71–0.76), then performs a long, deliberate fade from 3:35 to the quietest moment at 3:57 (0.16). The 43 dB range is wide for such a gentle piece, and most of that range is spent in the final 25 seconds.
dynamics_arc.climax_description: The climax centres on 2:23–2:25, measured at 2:23 with peak intensity 0.87 at 2:25. It is prepared by the darkest harmonic turn in the piece. D#m is held 3.5 s at 2:07, then A#7#5sus4 at 2:12 leads into the G#m9 walking bass at 2:14–2:15 and onto Bmaj7/F# at 2:16–2:19. That classic vi–(V/vi)–ii–IV approach makes the arrival on the tonic feel hard-won. At the peak itself F#6 and F# alternate (2:20, 2:21, 2:23, 2:24) in the densest texture of the piece, 2.15 attacks/s and about 24 notes/s, then the bass moves to a C# pedal (2:27–2:30) to sustain the tension. This is a radiant tonic summit coloured by the added-6th D#, the same pitch as the relative minor root that prepared it.

summary.texture_and_register: Throughout, the texture is built from rolled, many-note chords: notes-per-second runs about 7–10 times the attack rate. Each gesture is therefore a resonant bloom of maj7, maj9, add9 or sus2 colour rather than a melody with accompaniment. The overall register is low-centred (median C#3, range B1–G#5 overall, reaching C#6 in Section 4). Section 0 is confined to F#2–A#3, a dark pedal glow. Sections 1–3 open upward to A#4–D#5 while the bass deepens to B1, so the texture widens. Section 3 is the thickest, with a walking bass and inner-voice 9ths and 11ths. Section 4 is the airiest and brightest, with the highest notes and open fifth and sus2 voicings, and the coda settles back into the low-middle. Pedal tones (F# for most of the first two minutes, C# and D# later) are the textural foundation.
summary.emotional_narrative: The piece begins by simply laying down home: from 0:00 to 0:29 a low F# pedal glows with the leading tone E# rubbing against it, hushed and expectant. From 0:29 it opens gently. F#maj7 and F#maj9 bloom, and suspended dominant colours (C#11/F# at 0:45 and 0:49, C#13sus4/F# at 0:53) hover over the tonic without ever pushing it away. At 1:16 the bass finally moves to B, and the music widens into gratitude, the 4-second Bmaj7 at 1:45 leading to a 6.5-second rest on F# at 1:55. Then comes the real feeling. At 2:07 the relative minor D#m darkens the colour, G#m9 walks down at 2:14, and the music climbs to its summit at 2:23 on alternating F#6 and F#, full-hearted but bittersweet. Afterward, from 2:51, the voicings rise high and open on Bsus2 and Badd9 and end on a questioning C# major at 3:10–3:13. The coda from 3:15 shades the homecoming with D#m and Bmaj7/D#, revisits B and F#, then fades over 25 seconds onto F#/A#. Home is reached, but on its third, so the ending feels peaceful yet quietly open.

imagery_cues.light: Low amber light at the horizon that slowly brightens to a broad, even golden wash around 2:00–2:30. It turns briefly pale and high-white at 2:55–3:15, then sinks to a rose-gold dusk and blue-grey dimness at the close.
imagery_cues.motion: Slow, untethered drift with no metric snap. Long gliding pans and gentle dolly pushes that breathe with each rolled chord (about one gesture every half second, phrases every few seconds). Motion pauses on the long holds (1:45, 1:55, 2:07, 2:43) and pulls slowly back and upward during the final fade.
imagery_cues.scale: Intimate and close at the opening, the low pedal suggesting nearness. The frame widens to a human-scale landscape through Sections 1–2, becomes vast and sky-wide at the 2:23 climax and in the high, open Section 4, then returns to intimate stillness in the fading coda.
environments: a calm lake at dawn and again at dusk
rolling open fields under a widening sky
a quiet coastline with breaking cloud light
a high meadow beneath thin bright cirrus
a sunlit, empty wooden room with tall windows
imagery_cues.atmosphere: Mild and humid-soft air with low mist at the start that lifts through the middle. Moving clouds and breaking sun at the climax give way to a clear, thin, high sky. The close is a cooling, windless dusk.

summary.harmonic_highlights: Several labels reflect the tonic sound itself rather than separate chords. The recurring 'F/F#', 'A#/F#', 'A#5/F' and 'Fmb6b9/F#' (0:09–0:28 and throughout) are best read as F#maj7, with E# rubbing against the F# root. This leading-tone-against-tonic shimmer is the piece's harmonic fingerprint. Over the F# pedal, suspended dominants float without cadencing: C#11/F# at 0:45 and 0:49, and C#13sus4/F# at 0:53. The first real bass motion comes at 1:16–1:22, onto the B (IV) area via D#5/A# with the lowest note, B1. Across 1:31–1:43, F#maj9 and F#maj9/C# alternate, a root/second-inversion rocking. The big plagal arrival is Bmaj7 (4 s, 1:45) and Bmaj9 (1:49) leading to F# held 6.5 s at 1:55. The climax is prepared by D#m held 3.5 s at 2:07, then A#7#5sus4 at 2:12 as an ambiguous V/vi colour and G#m9 over a moving bass (B, D#, F#) at 2:14–2:15, landing on Bmaj7/F# at 2:16 and 2:19. The summit at 2:20–2:25 alternates F#6 and F#. The C# dominant pedal at 2:27–2:30 carries D#m11/C#, C#6add9 and F#maj9/C#. The half cadence on C# major at 3:10–3:13 is left open. In the coda, a D# bass at 3:15–3:21 supports D#m and Bmaj7/D#. At 3:26 the C# dominant moves deceptively to B (3:29–3:35), not F#. The final chord is F#/A#, first inversion, held from 3:50, an unresolved homecoming.
summary.rhythm_and_feel: The piece is in free time and rubato throughout: pulse clarity 0.04 and steadiness 0.13 mean there is no reliable beat to tap, despite the nominal 70 BPM tactus. Gestures are rolled chords at about 1.6–2.4 attacks per second, each sounding many notes. Harmonic rhythm is fluid. Colours shift every 1–2 s in the active passages, but structural arrivals are stretched into long fermata-like holds (Bmaj7 4 s at 1:45, F# 6.5 s at 1:55, D#m 3.5 s at 2:07, F#maj7 3 s at 2:43, F#/A# from 3:50). The climax is both the densest passage (2.15 attacks/s) and the slowest local tempo (67.4 BPM), a broadening rather than a rushing. The coda has slightly more frequent attacks (2.38/s) but lighter touch, giving a murmuring, settling feel as it fades.
summary.relearning_tips: 1. Start with the home sound: hold a low F#2–C#3 fifth in the left hand. In the right hand, voice E#–F#–A#–C# for the F#maj7 shimmer and add G# for F#maj9. Most of the 'F/F#' and 'Fmb6b9' labels are this sound, so confirm by ear that the E#-against-F# rub is intentional. 2. Learn the suspended dominant over the pedal at 0:45–0:53: keep F# in the bass and play C#sus / B-major-over-C# shapes (C#–F#–G#–B–D#) in the right hand for C#11 and C#13sus4. 3. Practise the IV area as a separate block: B1 or B2 bass with Badd9 / Bsus2 (1:19–1:22), then the spread Bmaj7 to Bmaj9 at 1:45–1:52 resolving plagally to F# at 1:55. Give that F# its full 6.5 s. 4. Drill the climax chain slowly and in time: D#m (2:07), A#7sus colour (2:12), G#m9 with the bass walking B–D#–F# (2:14–2:15), Bmaj7/F# (2:16), then F#6 alternating with F# (2:20–2:24) and C# pedal chords (2:27–2:30). Once it is secure, add rubato. 5. Treat Section 4 as voicing study: open fifths and sus2 shapes in the high register, with the C# major half-cadence at 3:10 voiced bright and left ringing. 6. Learn the coda last: the D#m and Bmaj7/D# alternation (3:15–3:21), the deceptive C# to B move (3:26–3:29) and the vi–I circling at 3:40–3:49, ending on F#/A#. Practise the final 25-second diminuendo deliberately, since the piece's widest dynamic range lives there. Throughout, roll chords from the bass upward and let the pedal carry resonance between gestures rather than counting beats.

sections.name: Pedal Dawn
sections.description: The piece opens low and quiet on an F# pedal (F#2–A#3, median F#2). The C/A label at 0:01 is almost certainly a transcription artefact of the first attack. From 0:09 the core sound establishes itself. F#maj7 alternates with its upper-structure shapes: A#/F# at 0:09 and 0:15, A#5/F at 0:10 and 0:16, and F/F#, held 1.5 s at 0:17. All of these are the same idea, E# (the major 7th) and A# / C# shimmering against the F# root. At 0:22 a G#/F# and F#/G#/A# cluster adds the 9th, settling into F#add9 at 0:23 and F#sus2 (held 1.5 s) at 0:26. The Fmb6b9/F# labels at 0:25 and 0:28 are again the E#-against-F# rub. Texture is rolled chords in the bass-tenor range with almost no melody, a statement of the tonic colour itself.
sections.character: A low, hushed tonic pedal that glows rather than speaks, the leading tone hovering against the root like light not yet risen.
sections.dynamics: Quiet (about -34.6 dBFS, 0.31 intensity at 0:00), building gradually to about 0.5 by 0:20–0:25.
sections.texture: Sparse rolled chords over a sustained F# pedal; close maj7 voicings in a single low register band.
sections.register: Low: bass on F#2, voicings topping out around A#3; no upper register yet.
sections.emotional_beat: Arrival and settling, the home chord is laid down as ground before anything is said.
sections.imagery: A dim, still lake before sunrise, the far shore just a low band of warm grey with a faint amber seam along the horizon.
sections.label: Pedal Dawn (0:00-0:29)

sections.name: Suspended Dominant Glow
sections.description: The texture lifts into the middle register (F#2–A#4, median C#3) as the tonic grows richer. There is F# at 0:29, F#maj7 held 2 s at 0:30 and F#maj9 held 1.5 s at 0:33, then F# held 2 s at 0:36 with F#add9 at 0:40 and 0:42. From 0:44 the first real harmonic motion arrives, though the F# pedal stays put. G#/B leads to C#11/F# (1.5 s) at 0:45, then F#sus24 at 0:46, then C#11/F# again (1.5 s) at 0:49, then C#13sus4/F# at 0:53. This is a suspended dominant floating over the tonic bass, the signature Barnoski move of dominant colour that never pushes to a cadence. Around 0:56–0:58 the transcription flickers between A#mb6b9/F# and F#add9, which is most likely F#maj9 with the melody circling A#–B–C#. A first touch of the relative minor follows at 1:02 (D#m9/F) and 1:05 (D#madd9/F#), before F#maj7 is held 2 s at 1:09. At 1:15 A#/B and D#5 begin steering the bass toward B for the next section.
sections.character: Gently opening and tender, with dominant suspensions shimmering above an unmoving tonic floor.
sections.dynamics: mp, steady around 0.5–0.68 intensity (about -28 dBFS), with small swells at 0:35–0:50 and 1:15.
sections.texture: Rolled maj7/maj9 voicings over the F# pedal with a soft inner melodic line emerging in the right hand; dominant upper structures layered over the tonic bass.
sections.register: Low-middle: bass on F#2, voicings centred around C#3–F#3, melody reaching A#4.
sections.emotional_beat: The first breath of feeling, warmth spreading outward and the music beginning to reach.
sections.imagery: Pale gold light spreading slowly across calm water, mist lifting in thin layers off its surface.
sections.label: Suspended Dominant Glow (0:29-1:16)

sections.name: Subdominant Opening
sections.description: The bass finally moves. Via D#5/A# and A#/B/D# (1:16–1:17) it arrives on B, with B5, B, Badd9 and Bsus2 at 1:19–1:22, reaching the lowest note of the piece, B1. This IV area opens the space before returning to F# at 1:24 (held 1.5 s at 1:24 and 1:27). The heart of the section is an extended F#maj9 passage alternating between root position and second inversion (F#maj9 and F#maj9/C#) at 1:31–1:43. That swing in the bass between F# and C# creates a gentle rocking motion, with a fleeting A#m7 colour at 1:39. A cluster at 1:44 (F#/B/G#/A#) leads to the section's big gesture, Bmaj7 held a full 4 s at 1:45. Bmaj9 (2 s) follows at 1:49 with D#m and D#m7 in the inner voices at 1:49 and 1:51, then Bmaj9/F#. The section lands in a plagal IV–I arrival on F#, held 6.5 s from 1:55, the longest hold in the piece.
sections.character: Broadening and luminous, the Bmaj7–Bmaj9 plateau opening the harmony like a widening view before a long, contented rest on the tonic.
sections.dynamics: mf, intensity 0.67–0.76 (about -24.4 dBFS), peaking around 1:50 on the Bmaj9, then easing to 0.59 at 2:00 during the long F# hold.
sections.texture: Fuller rolled voicings with a moving bass (F#–C# alternation, B pedal); wide spread between low bass and right-hand maj9 colour.
sections.register: Low to middle-high: bass dropping to B1, voicings centred on F#3, melody up to C#5.
sections.emotional_beat: Expansion and gratitude, the music finds its open space and rests in it.
sections.imagery: A wide valley opening at the crest of a hill, late-morning light pouring evenly across rolling fields.
sections.label: Subdominant Opening (1:16-2:05)

sections.name: Bittersweet Summit
sections.description: This is the climax, beginning with F#6 at 2:05 and turning straight to the relative minor: D#m/F# at 2:06, then D#m held 3.5 s from 2:07. That held vi is the most decisive minor moment of the piece. A#7#5sus4 at 2:12 (an ambiguous label, likely the V/vi colour leaning back toward D#m or G#m) leads into G#m9 with a descending or shifting bass at 2:14–2:15 (G#m9/B, /D#, /F#). That ii9 with a walking bass then settles onto Bmaj7/F# (1.5 s) at 2:16 and 2:19. The peak is reached as F#6 and F# alternate at 2:20–2:25, F# held 2 s at 2:21 and 2:24, with the measured climax at 2:23 and intensity 0.87 at 2:25. The bass then shifts to a C# dominant pedal at 2:27–2:30 (D#m11/C#, C#6add9, D#7sus4/C#, F#maj9/C#) and a brief G# bass at 2:32 before re-centring. The release comes through F#add9 at 2:34, D#m7add11/C# at 2:36, F#sus2 at 2:40, F#maj7 held 3 s at 2:43 and F# held 3 s at 2:47.
sections.character: Full-hearted and bittersweet, the brightest swell of the piece arrives through the relative minor, so the peak feels earned and slightly aching rather than triumphant.
sections.dynamics: f at its loudest: about -22.3 dBFS, intensity 0.82 at 2:10 rising to 0.87 at 2:25, then receding to about 0.58 by 2:45.
sections.texture: The densest passage: 2.15 attacks/s and 24 notes/s of thick rolled chords, a moving bass line (G#–B–D#–F#) and C#/G# pedal points under rich 9th and 11th voicings.
sections.register: Middle, centred around F3: bass from D#2, melody reaching D#5.
sections.emotional_beat: The emotional summit, love and longing in the same breath as the minor shading touches the major peak.
sections.imagery: Sun breaking through a bank of cloud over the sea, shafts of light and shadow moving together across the water.
sections.label: Bittersweet Summit (2:05-2:51)

sections.name: High Suspended Light
sections.description: After the climax the texture thins and lifts. The spectral centroid is the brightest of the piece (about 470 Hz), and the register reaches C#6, the highest note. The harmony rests on suspended subdominant colour: F#5 at 2:53, then Bsus2, Badd9, B (1.5 s), B5 (1.5 s) and B again across 2:53–2:57, Bsus2 returning at 3:00. C#7sus4/B at 3:01 blends dominant and subdominant, then F#add9/C# and F# at 3:01–3:02 give a lingering tonic held to about 3:07. G#/F# at 3:07 and F#sus2 (1.5 s) at 3:08 lead to the section's goal, a held C# major chord at 3:10–3:13, clear in root position and with G# bass at 3:11. This is an open half-cadence on V that leaves the tonic in question. The Fmb6b9/C# at 3:13 is likely C# with suspended or upper-voice colour. Suspensions make up 23% of the section, the highest share of any section.
sections.character: Airy and questioning, a high, open-voiced afterglow that ends on the dominant rather than coming home.
sections.dynamics: mf, steady around 0.6–0.74 intensity (about -25.8 dBFS), with a second, smaller swell building from 3:05 toward 3:15–3:20.
sections.texture: Thinner, open fifth and sus2 voicings with sparkling high right-hand notes; less bass weight, more air between the hands.
sections.register: Widest span of the piece: bass B1, median C#3, top notes reaching C#6.
sections.emotional_beat: Afterglow and question, the summit has passed and the music looks upward and outward instead of resolving.
sections.imagery: High thin clouds catching the last bright light over an open plain, the sky pale and vast.
sections.label: High Suspended Light (2:51-3:15)

sections.name: Unresolved Homecoming
sections.description: The coda turns to the relative minor in its opening seconds, with D#m (1.5 s) at 3:15. Bmaj7/D# (2 s) follows at 3:17, and D#m and Bmaj7/D# alternate at 3:19 over a D# bass, then D#m7 at 3:21. This is vi and IV sharing the same pitch world, a tender, shadowed colour. F#5 (2 s) at 3:22 and F#sus2 lead to C#sus4 and then C# (2 s) at 3:25–3:26, a dominant that this time does move on. It moves to B, though, not F#: B5, B6, B (1.5 s), Badd9 and B6add9 (1.5 s) across 3:29–3:35. F# returns at 3:36–3:39 (F#6add9, F#add9, F#6). The final descent circles vi against I: D#m7add11, D#m7/C#, D#m and Bmaj7/D# at 3:40–3:44, then F#/C#, D#m/F#, Bmaj7/F# and F# at 3:44–3:49. The piece settles at 3:50 on F#/A#, the tonic in first inversion with A# in the bass, held and fading to silence. The B/C/D# at 3:57 is decay noise.
sections.character: Tender and quietly bittersweet, coming home but leaving the door ajar: the final tonic sits on its third rather than its root.
sections.dynamics: Begins still warm (about 0.73–0.76 at 3:20–3:25), then a long diminuendo: 0.59 at 3:40, 0.4 at 3:45, 0.25 at 3:50, down to the quietest moment, 0.16, at 3:57–4:00 (section average -40.7 dBFS).
sections.texture: Gentle rolled chords at 2.38 attacks/s, with lighter touch (mean velocity 51) and a slow alternation of vi and I shapes over shifting D#, C#, F# and A# bass notes, thinning into a single sustained chord.
sections.register: Low-middle: bass from B1, median C#3, melody up to F#5, ending in the middle register on F#/A#.
sections.emotional_beat: Letting go, home is reached but held lightly, with an aftertaste of longing in the open, first-inversion ending.
sections.imagery: Dusk settling over the same still lake from the opening, a last rose-gold line on the water slowly fading into blue-grey.
sections.label: Unresolved Homecoming (3:15-4:02)

tempo.description: It feels slow and breathing rather than metred. The measured tactus is 70.1 BPM (alternative level 35), but pulse clarity is only 0.04 and steadiness 0.13, so it is essentially rubato in free time. Attacks arrive about 1.9 per second, while transcribed notes run 12–24 per second. That gap means each gesture is a rich, rolled or arpeggiated chord rather than a stream of single notes, and the ear hears waves of resonance, not beats. Harmonic rhythm is mostly one colour change every 1–2 s. It broadens at cadential arrivals into long holds: Bmaj7 for 4 s at 1:45, F# for 6.5 s at 1:55, D#m for 3.5 s at 2:07 and F#maj7 for 3 s at 2:43. These holds make the felt tempo closer to the 35 BPM level in the most spacious moments. Local tempo eases from 77 BPM in the opening to about 67 BPM at the climax, a subtle broadening into the peak.

mode_balance.evidence: The music is decisively major. By held duration it is 68% major chords, 15% minor, 2% dominant and 7% suspended (minor-weight 0.07). The major colour is enriched rather than plain. The maj7 and maj9 sonorities (F#maj7, F#maj9, Bmaj7, Bmaj9) and add9 / sus2 voicings carry a Lydian-tinged openness on IV but no true modal borrowing; no modal colours were detected and there are no borrowed iv or bVII chords. The minor content is diatonic: D#m (vi), G#m9 (ii, at 2:14–2:15) and A#m7 (iii, a fleeting moment at 1:39). It concentrates in the climax, which is 24% minor, and the coda, which is 26% minor, adding a bittersweet shade at exactly the most emotional points. Suspensions are structurally important. There is F#sus2 at 0:26, 1:00, 2:40 and 3:08, C#11 and C#13sus4 over F# at 0:45–0:53, and Bsus2 in Section 4, which is 23% suspended. Together they reflect suspension over resolution: the major key is stated but often left hovering.

summary.overview: A slow, free-time meditation built almost entirely over a C pedal, in which a C major sonority keeps breathing in and out of its minor-plagal shadow, Fm6 / Fm6/9. Barnoski's signature language is everywhere: a held C/G bass, inner voices that lean G→A♭→G and E→F→E, and transcription 'chords' like Dm9♭5/F and E+add#9/G that are really those neighbour tones smeared across the pedal. Twice the music tips fully into C Aeolian at its loudest points (Cm, B♭, A♭maj7, Gm at 1:11–1:39 and 2:40–3:04), with the second wave peaking on a B♭ major chord at 2:58. It ends by suspending rather than cadencing, Gsus4 → Csus2 → Cadd9 → an 8.5-second C major. The emotional core is a major home that is haunted, but never overthrown, by its parallel minor.
summary.key_center: C major, though only weakly so (Krumhansl clarity 0.19, with C minor a close runner-up). C is less a key than a pedal: almost every section sits on C or C/G in the bass, and the harmony is defined by what hovers above it. Sections 0, 1, 3, 4 and 6 read as C major with constant borrowed iv (Fm6, Fm6/9, Fm13). Sections 2 (1:11–1:39) and 5 (2:40–3:04) are locally estimated as C minor and behave Aeolian: Cm (3.0 s at 1:29), Cm11/B♭, Gm (1:34), A♭maj7/C (1:38, 2:50–2:51, 3:03) and B♭ major (2:58, the climax). There is a brief tonicization of F via C7 at 1:16 → Fm(add9) at 1:18–1:19, which functions as V/iv. A backdoor B♭9/F → C/G arrives at 2:07–2:09. The C/E♭ ambiguity (C/D# ↔ D#/C at 1:39–1:43 and 2:41–2:44, C7#9 at 3:08) is the piece's central modal tension, resolved to major only in the coda.

mood.overall: A tender, haunted calm that twice gathers into a dark, heavy swell before settling back into a hushed and unresolved C major light.

dynamics_arc.description: The piece is a double wave with a rising overall shape, spanning 28.7 dB. It begins near-silent (intensity 0.17–0.23, 0:00–0:10) and climbs steadily through Section 1 to a first plateau of 0.73–0.78 between 1:15 and 1:35, coinciding with the turn to C minor. It recedes to about 0.45 around 1:55, during the major-key thaw, then holds near 0.53 through 2:25. A sharp surge (0.53 → 0.82 between 2:25 and 2:35) leads to the main plateau of 0.81–0.88 from 2:35 to 3:00. The release is sudden: 0.87 at 3:00 drops to 0.45 by 3:10, then fades gradually to 0.10 at 3:35. Loudness is consistently tied to low register and minor harmony. The loudest sections (2 and 5) are the lowest and most Aeolian, while the soft sections carry the major home and the high treble.
dynamics_arc.climax_description: The climax arrives at 2:58 on B♭ major (A#7 → A#M, 1.5 s) within the C-Aeolian Section 5. It is prepared by the rocking Cm7 ↔ E♭/C ostinato over the C pedal (2:41–2:44), a long A#sus2 (2:46) that opens without resolving, and a ♭VII → ♭VI descent to A♭maj7 (2:49–2:51). Fm13/C → Fm9/C (2:55–2:56) then pushes subdominant pressure into the B♭ arrival. Voicings sit in the lowest, densest register of the piece (median F3, 37.8 notes/s, −9.6 dBFS). Rather than resolving, the peak falls back through A♭ to Cm (3:03) and then collapses into the open fifth at 3:05.

summary.texture_and_register: The full range is C2–D6, centred low on A#3, and the bass rarely leaves C or G: the pedal tone is the spine of the whole piece. The texture is spacious arpeggiation (2.5 attacks/s) heavily blurred by sustain, so transcribed note density (10–38 notes/s) far exceeds the attack rate. Inner neighbour tones ring across the pedal and create the 'extended' labels (Dm9♭5/F, E+add#9/G, G#M6#11/F), which are really triads with ♭6/9/6 colour. Register and loudness are inversely matched to brightness. The quiet major sections (0, 3, 4) reach into the high treble (D6, F6, D#6) with a median around C4. The two loud minor sections (2, 5) drop the treble entirely, top out at C5 and sink to a median of G#3/F3, so the peaks feel deep and enveloping rather than bright. The coda keeps the low centre (G#3) but thins out, ending on a single resonant C chord.
summary.emotional_narrative: 0:00–0:37: a quiet C major tonic is introduced already in dialogue with its minor shadow Fm6, swinging gently back and forth over a held C/G, more question than statement. 0:37–1:11: the inner voices grow chromatic (B against A♭, a brush with B♭ and Gm at 0:44, a cluster at 0:54) and the music swells, as though something is waking beneath the surface. 1:11–1:39: through C7 → Fm (1:16–1:19), the shadow takes over, the tonic becomes Cm (1:29) and the bass walks the Aeolian path B♭–G–A♭ in a heavy, slowed, low-register mass. 1:39–2:10: the third flickers between E♭ and E until major returns (CM 1:51), reached gently through backdoor cadences (B♭7/A♭ → G → C at 1:56–1:58, B♭13/F → C/G at 2:07–2:09) rather than a firm dominant. 2:10–2:40: the home key reasserts itself with long C holds (2:28–2:33), but B♭ major at 2:34 and an A♭ bass signal that the shadow is gathering again. 2:40–3:04: the climax is a full-throated C Aeolian surge, rocking Cm7/E♭ over the pedal and cresting on B♭ major at 2:58, a moment where darkness itself glows. 3:04–3:39: an open fifth and a C7#9 hover between modes before C major settles (3:09). The original C–Fm6 loop returns softly, and the piece ends on Gsus4 → Csus2 → Cadd9 → C. Home is reached, but with suspensions in place of a final V–I, as if the ghost is allowed to stay.

imagery_cues.light: Diffuse, low pale light that dims and cools into slate-blue shadow at each swell. A single amber shaft breaks through at the 2:58 peak, then everything settles into faint violet twilight.
imagery_cues.motion: Slow, drifting, unmetred camera glides with no cuts on a beat. Motion swells in long breaths roughly every 7 seconds, following the C ↔ Fm6 cycle. The camera sinks lower and heavier during the minor surges (1:11–1:39, 2:40–3:04) and comes nearly to rest on the final held C.
imagery_cues.scale: Intimate at the opening, expanding to a vast, enveloping scale at 1:15–1:35 and again at 2:35–3:00, then contracting to close and still for the coda.
environments: an empty old house with tall windows at dawn
a wide grey lake under shifting cloud
a stormy coastline at dusk
a stone cellar with pooled light
a fog-covered meadow at twilight
imagery_cues.atmosphere: Cool, damp, misty air that thickens into heavy storm cloud at the peaks and clears to a calm, rain-washed stillness at the end.

chord_vocabulary: C with A♭ neighbour (labelled E+add#9/G, Emb6b9/G)
summary.harmonic_highlights: Pedal point: C (often C/G) underpins nearly the entire piece, and the labelled 'extensions' are mostly upper neighbours sounding over it. Minor plagal core: C → Fm6 at 0:01–0:04, recurring throughout and returning in the coda at 3:18–3:26. The ♭6–5 neighbour (A♭ against G) explains the 'augmented' labels: E+add#9/G at 0:07 and 0:38, G#aug at 0:49 and 3:24, and the E7#5#9/G cluster at 2:10–2:16. First Aeolian glimpse: B♭/Gm colour at 0:44. Secondary dominant: C7 (1:16) → Fm(add9) (1:18–1:19) tonicizes iv just before the minor descent. Tonic goes minor: Cm held 3.0 s at 1:29, then the bass steps down through Cm11/B♭ (1:32), Gm (1:34), G5/D (1:35) and A♭maj7/C (1:38). Third ambiguity: C/E♭ ↔ E♭/C at 1:39–1:43 and 2:41–2:44, C+add#9 at 1:43, and C7#9 at 3:08. Backdoor cadences: rootless B♭7/A♭ → G5 → Cadd9/G at 1:56–1:58, and B♭9/F → B♭13/F → C/G at 2:07–2:09. ♭VII foreshadowing: B♭ major held 2.0 s at 2:34. The climax resolves to ♭VII rather than V: B♭7 → B♭ at 2:57–2:58, then A♭ → Cm at 3:00–3:03. A Picardy-like turn at 3:09 sets CM after the Cm of 3:03. Suspended final cadence: Gsus4 → Csus2 → Cadd9 → C (3:27–3:29), with no true dominant-seventh resolution anywhere in the piece, which is suspension over resolution in its purest form.
summary.rhythm_and_feel: Free-time rubato with a loose 54 BPM tactus (pulse clarity 0.14) and an eighth-note arpeggio subdivision near 108 BPM. Attacks are spaced at about 2.5/s, quite steady across sections (2.26–3.03/s). Intensity therefore grows through voicing weight, register and pedal saturation rather than faster playing. Harmonic rhythm is slow and breathing: about one real harmony every 3–4 s in the opening loop, roughly three beats per chord, which suggests a lilting compound or triple feel. It stretches further at structural arrivals: Cm for 3 s at 1:29, CM for 2.5 s at 1:51 and 2:31, B♭ for 2 s at 2:34, and the final C for 8.5 s. Section 2 broadens (local 41.5 BPM) and Section 3 eases forward (63 BPM). The climax returns to around 57 BPM with a rocking two-chord C/E♭ ostinato that gives the only near-regular pulse in the piece.
summary.relearning_tips: 1) Start with the core loop at 0:01–0:14. Hold C2/G2 in the left hand and move the right hand from C–E–G(–C) to F–A♭–C–D (Fm6), keeping C as a common tone and voicing E→F and G→A♭ as inner neighbours. Practise it slowly in pairs of about three beats each until the swing feels like breathing. 2) Add the colour variants: Fm6/9 (add G on top), Fm7add13 over F (F–A♭–C–E♭–D, the 'G#M6#11/F' label), and Cadd9/Fsus2. Let the A♭ overlap the G briefly, which is the E+add#9/G sound and is intentional colour, not a mistake. 3) Learn the minor descent at 1:11–1:39 as a bass line: C (C7, V/iv) → F → C → C (Cm) → B♭ → G → D → A♭ → C, voicing Cm11/B♭, Gm and A♭maj7/C with open fifths low and thirds/sevenths in the middle register (below C5). 4) Isolate the two backdoor cadences, rootless B♭7/A♭ (A♭–D–F) → G → Cadd9/G at 1:56–1:58 and B♭9/F → B♭13/F → C/G at 2:07–2:09, which are the gentle bridges back to major. 5) Learn the climax at 2:40–3:04: the rocking Cm7 ↔ E♭/C figure over the C pedal, then B♭sus2 → A♭maj7 → Cm → Fm13/C → B♭7 → B♭ (2:58) → A♭ → Cm. Keep it low and full, building with weight and pedal rather than speed. 6) Finish with the coda cadence C5 → Gsus4 → Csus2 → Cadd9 → C and let the last chord ring 8 s or more. Practice order: core loop, coda, Section 3 backdoors, Section 2 descent, then the climax. Treat transcription labels such as Gb9sus (2:20), C#maj9/C (1:08) and the 0:54–0:56 cluster as ambiguous and check them against the recording.
summary.title: KB_GHOST_REF_2.0

sections.name: Pedal and Shadow
sections.description: The piece opens on C/G (0:01) and immediately leans into Fm6 (0:04, held 3.0 s), establishing the core gesture: C major ↔ minor iv over a sustained G/C bass. The labels E+add#9/G (0:07) and Emb6b9/G (0:10) are passing moments where the inner A♭ (♭6) overlaps the G of the C triad on its way back to CM/G (0:08, 0:14). Fm6/9 (0:17, 0:19, 0:30) and G#M6#11/F (0:24, 0:31 = F–A♭–C–E♭–D, essentially Fm7 add 13) deepen the subdominant colour. Fsus2 (0:04, 0:17) and CMadd9 (0:22) add open, Barnoski-style 2/9 colour. The loop cycles roughly every 7 s (C → Fm → C), with a high melody reaching up to D6 over a median of C4.
sections.character: A quiet question asked over and over: home, then its shadow, then home again.
sections.dynamics: pp–p (−30 dBFS), with a gentle swell from intensity 0.17 at 0:05 to 0.41 by 0:20 that then hovers.
sections.texture: Spacious arpeggiated chords over a held C/G pedal; a sparse treble line floats above sustained inner neighbour motion.
sections.register: Middle with high glints: bass on F2–G2, harmony around C4, melody touching up to D6.
sections.emotional_beat: Establishing the home and its ghost: the major tonic is never heard without the minor iv leaning against it.
sections.imagery: Pale early light falling through a tall window onto bare floorboards, dust slowly turning in the beam.
sections.label: Pedal and Shadow (0:00-0:37)

sections.name: Restless Inner Voices
sections.description: The same C/G ↔ Fm loop continues (CM/G 0:39, 0:46, 0:51; Fm6 1:00–1:01; Fm6/9 0:54), but the inner voices grow more chromatic. B/C/D and B/G# (0:42) suggest a leading-tone B against A♭, and A#13b5/G with Gm/D (0:44) brushes the Aeolian ♭VII/v area for the first time. Am/ma7/E (0:47) and G#aug (0:49) reflect the A–A♭ chromatic line descending toward Fm. A cluster at 0:54–0:56 (B/D/A#/A, C#sus2/D#) is the densest chromatic moment so far, quickly reabsorbed into Emb6b9/C → CM (0:57–0:59). The section ends with C5 (1:03, an open fifth, mode-neutral), C7#5sus4 (1:06) and C#maj9/C (1:08, a D♭ colour over the C pedal). This is a Phrygian-flavoured lean that prepares the minor turn.
sections.character: The calm loop starts to churn from within, as if something beneath the surface is stirring.
sections.dynamics: p rising to mf: intensity climbs from 0.47 (0:40) to 0.62 (1:05), with loudness up 9 dB from the opening.
sections.texture: Fuller arpeggiation (18 notes/s) with more chromatic inner lines; the bass descends to C2 and the treble drops back below F5.
sections.register: Lower-middle: bass C2, centre C4, top around F5. The high register is abandoned and weight shifts downward.
sections.emotional_beat: Unrest: the shadow chords start to multiply and press on the home key.
sections.imagery: Clouds thickening over a wide grey lake, the water's surface beginning to ripple without wind.
sections.label: Restless Inner Voices (0:37-1:11)

sections.name: Descent into Minor
sections.description: At 1:11 the music turns: E7#5#9/C (1:15) acts as a chromatic pivot into C7 (1:16, 1.5 s), a real secondary dominant resolving to Fm(add9) at 1:18–1:19 (V/iv → iv). After a brief CM/CMadd9 (1:21–1:22) and another Fm6 → Fm6/9 → Fm13/C pass (1:24–1:26), the tonic itself goes minor. Cmadd9/Cm takes over from 1:27, with Cm held 3.0 s at 1:29. The bass then moves stepwise through the Aeolian descent: Cm11/B♭ (1:32), B♭6/Gm (1:33–1:34), G5/D (1:35, 1:5 s), Ddim/G# (1:37, best read as a rootless B♭7/A♭), and A♭maj7/C (1:38). The local tempo slows to 41.5 BPM while note density doubles to 34.9/s, creating a heavy, pedalled cloud in a low register (median G#3).
sections.character: The ghost takes the room: a dark, weighty minor passage that broadens rather than hurries.
sections.dynamics: mf–f (−14 dBFS), peaking at intensity 0.78 around 1:30 and holding there until 1:35.
sections.texture: Dense, pedal-blurred low arpeggios and full chords; the treble is withdrawn, leaving a thick middle-low mass.
sections.register: Low: bass C2–D2, median G#3, nothing above C5. This is the darkest register zone of the first half.
sections.emotional_beat: The first confrontation: the parallel minor fully surfaces and the home tonic darkens to Cm.
sections.imagery: A deep stone cellar where low light pools on wet walls and the air is thick and still.
sections.label: Descent into Minor (1:11-1:39)

sections.name: Ambiguous Thaw
sections.description: The bass keeps C while the third flickers: C/D# ↔ D#/C (1:39–1:43, Cm7 or E♭/C) gives way to C+add#9 (1:43, with both E and E♭ present) and back to Cm (1:45) and A♭maj7 (1:46). Then major breaks through: CM at 1:47 and 1:50, settling into CM held 2.5 s at 1:51. The Fm6 family returns as Dm9♭5/F (1:55, 2:00) and Dm7♭5/G# → Ddim/G# (1:56–1:57), which is iv moving to a rootless B♭7. This resolves through G5 → CMadd9/G (1:57–1:58), a soft ♭VII7 → V → I. A clearer backdoor cadence closes the section: A#9/F → A#13/F (B♭9/B♭13 over F, 2:07–2:08) → CM/G (2:09).
sections.character: Light returns hesitantly, with the third of the chord unable to decide between E♭ and E before choosing major.
sections.dynamics: Recedes from f to mp: intensity falls from 0.68 (1:40) to 0.45 (1:55), then edges back up to 0.53 by 2:10.
sections.texture: Thinner (2.26 attacks/s, the sparsest section) with sustained chords and a melody that rises back into the upper register.
sections.register: Wide: bass C2, centre C4, with the melody reaching F6, the highest point of the piece.
sections.emotional_beat: Aftermath and reconciliation: the major home is reclaimed through soft backdoor cadences rather than a strong dominant.
sections.imagery: Frost slowly melting off a windowpane as thin sun breaks through low cloud.
sections.label: Ambiguous Thaw (1:39-2:10)

sections.name: Second Gathering
sections.description: The opening's chromatic neighbour figure returns, now more insistent. E7#5#9/G and E+add#9/G (2:10–2:16) are C major with A♭ grinding against G, repeated several times over C/G. Fm13 (2:15, 2:19), FmM9/G (2:16) and Fm6/9 (2:20, 2:26) keep the minor iv in rotation. The section settles onto its longest tonic holds, CM 2.0 s (2:28), CM 2.5 s (2:31) and CMadd9 (2:33), before stepping to B♭ major (A#69#11 → A#M, 2:34, 2.0 s). This ♭VII is the first full-weight Aeolian major chord, previewing the climax. Bb/F (Dm#5/F, 2:36) → Ddim/G# → Dm7b5/G# (rootless B♭7/A♭) → Fm6 → A♭6 (2:37–2:39) carries the bass down through A♭ into the climax.
sections.character: The home key gathers strength, but each arrival on C is shadowed by B♭ and A♭ waiting in the wings.
sections.dynamics: mp building to f: intensity rises from 0.53 to 0.56 (2:15), holds near 0.53, then surges to 0.70 at 2:30 and 0.82 by 2:35.
sections.texture: Fuller arpeggiation (30 notes/s) over the pedal; long sustained tonic chords give way to a stepwise bass descent B♭ → A♭.
sections.register: Middle with high reach: bass C2, centre C4, melody up to D#6.
sections.emotional_beat: Gathering resolve: major asserts itself one more time before the floor gives way to the minor climax.
sections.imagery: Wind rising across a hilltop meadow, tall grass bending in long waves under a darkening sky.
sections.label: Second Gathering (2:10-2:40)

sections.name: Aeolian Summit
sections.description: The climax sits low and loud in C Aeolian. Fm13/C (2:40) leads into a rocking C/D# ↔ D#/C oscillation (2:41–2:44), Cm7 against E♭/C over the pedal, which acts as the section's ostinato. A#sus2 (2:46, 2.0 s) → B♭add9 → A♭6#11 → A♭maj7 (2:49–2:51) descends ♭VII → ♭VI. Then Cm (2:52), F5/C, and Fm13/C → Fm9/C (2:55–2:56) build into B♭7 → B♭ major at 2:58, the measured climax. The peak is a bright ♭VII chord rather than a dominant: Aeolian light at the darkest point. The tail falls back through B♭/F (Dm7#5/F) and A♭(add9) (3:00–3:01) to A♭maj7/C and Cm (3:03, 1.5 s).
sections.character: An overwhelming, heavy surge where grief and grandeur coexist, and the peak lifts on B♭ instead of resolving.
sections.dynamics: f–ff (−9.6 dBFS, 99% of range); intensity holds 0.81–0.88 from 2:35, peaks at 2:55–3:00 (climax at 2:58), and starts dropping just after 3:03.
sections.texture: The densest writing of the piece (37.8 notes/s): heavy low chords with a rocking C–E♭ figure, sustained-pedal resonance and full-hand voicings.
sections.register: Lowest of the piece: bass C2, median F3, nothing above C5. The climax deepens rather than brightens.
sections.emotional_beat: The full reckoning: the minor shadow becomes the whole sky, and the B♭ lift at 2:58 is its moment of terrible beauty.
sections.imagery: A vast slate-grey sea under storm clouds, one shaft of light breaking through onto heaving dark water.
sections.label: Aeolian Summit (2:40-3:04)

sections.name: Suspended Homecoming
sections.description: The collapse is immediate. A bare C5 (3:05, open fifth, neither major nor minor) is followed by A♭ (3:07) and C7#9 (3:08), with E and E♭ sounding together as a last flicker of ambiguity. Then CM at 3:09 settles the third on E, functioning like a Picardy turn. The opening loop returns softly: Dm9♭5/F → Fm (3:13–3:14), CM/G (3:17), Fm6 1.5 s (3:18), Fm6/9 (3:20), CM/G 2.0 s (3:22), G#aug → Fm6 (3:24) → Fm6/9 (3:26). The ending avoids any true V–I: C5 → Gsus4 (3:27) → Csus2 (3:28) → CMadd9 (3:29) → CM held 8.5 s, dying to the quietest point at 3:34.
sections.character: A soft return home where the shadow chord still visits, and the final cadence floats on suspensions rather than landing.
sections.dynamics: Falls from f to ppp: intensity 0.62 (3:05) → 0.42 (3:15) → 0.26 (3:30) → 0.10 (3:35). The final C fades into silence.
sections.texture: Sparse, slow arpeggios over a C pedal, thinning to a single sustained Cadd9/C chord ringing out.
sections.register: Low-middle and darker in tone (centroid 419 Hz, the darkest of the piece): bass C2, median G#3, top around F5.
sections.emotional_beat: Homecoming with memory: major wins, but the Fm6 shadow is kept as part of the house rather than banished.
sections.imagery: Twilight settling over a still pond after rain, the last light fading off the water's surface.
sections.label: Suspended Homecoming (3:04-3:39)

tempo.description: The measured tactus is 54.4 BPM, but pulse clarity is only 0.14 and steadiness 0.66, so it feels like free, breathing rubato rather than a beat. The 108.8 BPM alternative is best heard as the eighth-note subdivision of the arpeggiated figures. Attacks average just 2.53/s, so the ear gets a new event roughly every 0.4 s, gently spaced. The real harmonic rhythm is slower still. In the opening, the C ↔ Fm6 swing takes about 3–4 s per chord (CM/G 0:01 → Fm6 0:04 → CM/G 0:08 → Fm6 0:11 → CM/G 0:14), which is roughly one harmony per three beats. Section 2 feels heaviest and slowest (local tempo 41.5 BPM) even though it is loud, because the pedal-blurred note density doubles (34.9 notes/s) while attacks stay near 3/s. Section 3 lightens to a local 63 BPM, a slight easing forward after the first peak. The coda's final C is held for 8.5 s, and time effectively stops.

mode_balance.evidence: Major holds 49% of held duration against 26% minor, with 13% diminished/augmented, 3% dominant and 3% suspended (minor-weight 0.37). That makes the piece major-leaning, but the minor shading is structural rather than decorative. The diminished share is mostly the minor iv in disguise: Dm7♭5 = F–A♭–C–D = Fm6, and Dm9♭5/F simply adds E over it. Section 3's '24% diminished' therefore means Fm6 colour, not diminished function. The augmented labels (E+add#9/G, G#aug, C+add#9) are the A♭ neighbour sounding against C–E–G, i.e. ♭6 rubbing against 5. Borrowed ♭3 and ♭6 are explicit: C/E♭ oscillations (1:39, 2:41), A♭maj7 (1:46, 2:50), B♭ (♭VII) at 2:34 and 2:58, and Cm at 1:29 and 3:03. In the minor-estimated sections the 'major' chords are B♭, A♭ and E♭, borrowed from Aeolian, so those passages are darker than their 53% major share suggests. Final verdict: C major (Ionian) home with pervasive Aeolian mixture, resolving to pure major only at 3:09 and 3:29.

summary.overview: Cabin Soul 8 is a dense, low-centred piano meditation that lives in the ambiguous ground between Db major and F minor, which here is really F Phrygian. Most of its 'major' chords are upper-structure triads stacked over a bass pedal, so the music sounds warm but shadowed. Barnoski's signature is everywhere: Eb/F and Ab/F sonorities over a held F, Gb rubbing against F as a Phrygian ♭2, F-major (A-natural) flashes inside an F-minor world, and a Dbmaj13 opening. The emotional core is a long, steady plateau of churning, resonant intensity framed by a quiet Db-major invocation. It closes not on a tonic but on a suspended Eb6/9, choosing suspension over resolution.
summary.key_center: Bimodal and genuinely ambiguous; Krumhansl clarity is only 0.07, with F minor narrowly ahead of C# (Db) major. These are two readings of one collection: F Phrygian (F-Gb-Ab-Bb-C-Db-Eb) is the Db major scale. The opening section (0:00–0:21) and the first build (0:21–0:50) frame Db as home, starting with Dbmaj13 at 0:00, Eb7 at 0:05–0:07 and Db/Ab at 0:19. From 0:50 to 1:58 the centre of gravity shifts to an F pedal (local key F minor), with Eb/F, Ab/F (Fm7), Gb/F and F/A as the main colours. Tonicizations are brief. Eb7 (0:05) works as V/V or a Lydian II7 of Db. Db7, labelled C#/B (0:39, 1:01) and C#7 (1:42), leans toward Gb. Ab13sus4 (2:01) is a true V of Db, landing on Db at 2:02. The coda returns to Dbmaj7 (2:21) but ends on Eb6/9 → Eb5 (2:28–2:31), floating off-tonic. The most honest label is a Db major / F Phrygian axis, with F as the bass centre and Db as the harmonic 'roof'.

mood.overall: A warm but shadowed, inwardly surging reverie: resonant low harmony glowing like embers, with Phrygian half-step tension that never fully settles.

dynamics_arc.description: A long, flat-topped arch spanning 12.3 dB. It starts soft and slightly receding (0.49 → 0.38 by 0:10), then climbs steadily through 0:20–0:45 to reach 0.8 by 0:35. From 0:35 to 2:10 it holds a remarkably sustained plateau of 0.78–0.87 for over a minute and a half, more a sustained tide than a single peak. The release is late and fairly quick: 0.79 at 2:15, 0.63 at 2:20, 0.32 at 2:25 and 0.19 at 2:30, with the quietest moment at 2:28 on the final Eb6/9.
dynamics_arc.climax_description: The measured climax at 1:02 arrives on a Db13b9 over Ab (C#13b9/G#), prepared by Fm/C (0:58) → Dbmaj7/Ab (0:59, held 1.5 s) → Db7 (C#/B, 1:01). It releases into Eb/F (1:04) and Fm9/Ab (1:05), so the peak is a dominant-flavoured Db over its fifth, giving way to the F-pedal sonority. The plateau gains a second crest at 1:55–2:00 (0.87) during the Phrygian F/Gb and D7#9#11b13/F loop of section 3. That sustained second wave, more than a single blow, is what the coda finally releases.

summary.texture_and_register: Bass-heavy and resonant throughout: the overall range is F1–C5 with a median of C#3, so the centre of sound sits well below middle C and the melody rarely climbs above Db5. The texture is dense (about 4 attacks/s, 15–23 transcribed notes/s) and heavily pedalled. It is built from upper-structure triads over a sustained bass (Eb/F, Ab/F, Db/F, Gb/F), Barnoski's pedal-tone voicing language. The opening is the most spacious (2.57 attacks/s), with wide melodic leaps over held chords. Sections 1–3 thicken into continuous chordal arpeggiation, and section 3 lifts its median to F3 while adding the fastest motion. The coda thins to sustained Dbmaj7 and finally a bare Eb5, so the register stays low while the texture empties out.
summary.emotional_narrative: The piece opens (0:00–0:21) with a luminous Dbmaj13 and an Eb7 Lydian lift, a quiet naming of home that immediately glances at its shadows: F major (F/A, 0:12) and Gb (Gbsus2, 0:16). From 0:21 the harmony starts to move, with slash basses walking downward and borrowed colours like E/G# and Gbmaj7/F darkening the warmth into longing. Around 0:50 the floor shifts to an F pedal, and the music becomes a struggle between F minor (Fm7, 0:55–0:58), F major (F/A, 1:10) and the Phrygian Gb above (F/Gb, 1:06). That struggle crests at 1:02 on a Db13b9 over Ab. From 1:29 the churning intensifies rather than resolves, cycling F7#9, Fm7 and F/Gb over an insistent F bass and reaching its fullest energy around 1:55–2:00. At 1:58 a clear Ab13sus4 → Db cadence (2:01–2:02) offers a way home, and the long Dbmaj7 at 2:21 seems to accept it. Instead, the final gesture lifts to Eb9 over Db and ends on a suspended Eb6/9 fading to an open Eb5 (2:28–2:31). The story is of warmth that never quite settles: home is glimpsed, deeply felt, and left gently open.

imagery_cues.light: Low, warm firelight against cold blue dusk, steadily glowing through the middle and dimming to embers and twilight at the end.
imagery_cues.motion: Slow, breathing forward drift at a walking pace (about 92 BPM, elastic), gathering into a steady circling sway through the plateau and easing to near-stillness at the close; a subtle forward push matches the creeping tempo.
imagery_cues.scale: It begins intimate and close, widens to a human-scale enveloping warmth during the 0:35–2:10 plateau, and contracts again to a single quiet point of light at the end.
environments: a timber room at dusk with snow outside
a dark forest river under low cloud
a winter valley at last light
a stove-lit interior with frost-glazed windows
imagery_cues.atmosphere: Cold, still winter air outside held against a warm, close interior; soft snowfall that thickens into a swirling squall mid-piece and settles into calm, blue-violet twilight.

summary.harmonic_highlights: 0:00 Dbmaj13 (2.5 s): the home sonority, rich with the ninth and thirteenth. 0:05–0:07 Eb7 with add6/sus4: a Lydian II7 rather than a V/V, bright and unresolving. 0:12 F/A (2.0 s): the first Picardy-style F-major flash, a chromatic mediant against Db. 0:16 Gbsus2: the subdominant in suspended form. 0:29 and 0:48 E/G#, really Fb/Ab: a borrowed ♭III colour. 0:33 and 1:54 Gbmaj7/F: Gb major-seventh over an F bass, the defining Phrygian ♭2 sonority. 0:54–0:58 F7b5 → F → Fm7 → Fm7/Eb → Fm/C: the F-minor core stated plainly. 0:59–1:02 Dbmaj7/Ab → Db7 → Db13b9/Ab: the climax, Db functioning as dominant-flavoured ♭VI of F. 1:04 and 1:40 Eb/F: the signature pedal voicing, a triad a whole step below the bass. 1:15 and 2:12 A/F = Fmaj7#5: augmented shimmer. 1:38–1:39 F7#9 → F7: an A-natural against Ab blues clash on the pedal. 2:01–2:02 Ab13sus4 → Db: the piece's only clean authentic cadence. 2:25 Eb9 over Db: a Db Lydian (maj9#11) wash. 2:28–2:31 Eb6/9 → Eb5: an off-tonic suspended ending, a whole step above Db (or ♭VII of F), unresolved by design. Ambiguity note: labels like B/F (0:52), B7#5b9 (1:14) and D7#9#11b13/F (1:57) are probably overtone-inflated versions of Gb/F or F-pedal colours rather than literal chords.
summary.rhythm_and_feel: The elastic pulse sits around 92 BPM (an alternative 184 BPM double-time reading reflects the steady eighth-note motion). Pulse clarity of 0.37 means the beat is implied by flowing arpeggiation rather than accented, while steadiness of 0.81 keeps it from drifting. Surface harmonic rhythm is fast (labels change every 0.5–1 s), but the underlying bass pedals on F, Ab and Db move only every bar or two, giving a rocking, tidal feel. Melodic leaps recur every 2–4 seconds through 0:42, creating short phrase cells. The local tempo accelerates gradually from 89 to 99 BPM, so rubato pushes forward overall; the long-held chords at 0:00, 0:59, 2:21 and 2:28 act as breath points.
summary.relearning_tips: 1. Start with the pedal vocabulary over a low F (F1/F2 octave in the left hand). Cycle Eb/F → Ab/F (Fm7) → Gb/F → F/A → Db/F until the right-hand triad shapes are automatic; this covers most of 0:50–1:58. 2. Learn the bookends next: the Dbmaj13 opening voicing (Db–Ab low, with C, Eb, F and Bb above) and Eb7 (0:00–0:07), then the ending Dbmaj7 → Db(add9) → Eb9/Db → Eb6/9 → Eb5 (2:21–2:31). Let the final Eb hang without resolving. 3. Practise the climax approach slowly: Fm/C → Dbmaj7/Ab → Db/Cb → Db13b9/Ab → Eb/F (0:58–1:04), voicing the Ab bass firmly. 4. Isolate the F major/minor flip (Fmaj13 1:31, Fm(add4) 1:37, F7#9 1:38, F7 1:39) so the A-natural/Ab choice is deliberate. 5. Treat the transcription's quick passing labels as voice-leading between these anchor chords rather than separate harmonies. 6. Rehearse with awareness of the gradual tempo creep: decide whether you want the 89 → 99 BPM push or a steadier pulse, and keep the coda's diminuendo (2:15–2:30) unhurried even if the tempo leans forward.
summary.title: Cabin Soul 8

sections.name: Db Major Invocation
sections.description: The piece opens on a long Dbmaj13 (C#maj13, 0:00, 2.5 s), shimmering through Dbmaj7/Dbmaj9 inflections (0:02–0:04) with a C-to-Db rub in the bass (C#/C, C/C#). It moves to Eb7, with sus4 and add6 colours (0:05–0:07, 1.5 s), the bright II7 of Db Lydian. A chromatic slide follows (0:08–0:11: B/A#/D#, Ab/C, Ab/F, G/F#, F#/G) that settles on F/A at 0:12 (2.0 s), the first F-major Picardy glow. F6 (Dm/F, 0:15) and a Phrygian F/Eb → Gbsus2 (0:16) lead back to Db/F and Db/Ab (0:18–0:19), thinning to an open Db5 at 0:20. Melodic leaps are detected every 2–4 seconds, so the right hand states short, wide-interval cells over sustained bass.
sections.character: Spacious and questioning, like a statement of home colour that keeps glancing sideways at its F-major and Gb neighbours.
sections.dynamics: Moderately soft (−18.1 dBFS). It dips from 0.49 to 0.38 intensity by 0:10, then begins swelling to 0.61 by 0:20.
sections.texture: Sustained pedalled chords with wide leaping melodic cells; the sparsest section (2.57 attacks/s).
sections.register: Low-middle: bass reaching down to F1/Db2, harmony around C#3, melody peaking near D#4 (Eb4).
sections.emotional_beat: Arrival and quiet invocation: the home colour is named, along with the two shadows (F major and Gb) that will haunt it.
sections.imagery: Pale gold light gathering on a frost-dusted windowpane before dawn, the room still dark behind it.
sections.label: Db Major Invocation (0:00-0:21)

sections.name: Gathering Current
sections.description: Density jumps to 4.07 attacks/s and the surface harmony quickens into a stream of slash chords. Db and Eb alternate over C and Eb basses (0:22–0:25: Eb/C = Cm7, Db/C, Dbmaj9/Eb). A Dbsus/Db minor-major flicker at Ab arrives at 0:26. Colour then turns borrowed: E/G# (Fb/Ab, a ♭III colour) at 0:29 and 0:48, Gb/Bb and Gbmaj7b5 at 0:30, and Gbmaj7/F (F#mb6M7/F, 0:33), the first strong Phrygian ♭2 over the F bass. Ab/Gb and Ab/F (0:36–0:37) give way to Db/F and Db7 (C#/B, 0:38–0:39), then Gbmaj9/Ab and Fm(b6b9)/Ab (0:41) swirl around an Ab pedal. Eb7 at 0:47 and F#m9 → F/A at 0:49 hand off to the plateau. The melody keeps leaping (0:24–0:42) while the bass walks down through F, Eb, Db and Cb.
sections.character: The harmony begins to flow and darken, borrowed chords and slash basses pulling the Db home into restless motion.
sections.dynamics: A steady crescendo from about mp to mf (0.61 at 0:20 → 0.83 at 0:45), reaching −13.1 dBFS.
sections.texture: Busy pedalled arpeggiation over moving slash basses; layered inner voices with augmented and altered tints.
sections.register: Low centre of gravity (median C3), bass from F1, melody rising to G#4 (Ab4).
sections.emotional_beat: Departure and gathering: warmth turns into longing as the bass begins to travel.
sections.imagery: A dark river under overcast sky picking up speed, amber light flickering on its moving surface.
sections.label: Gathering Current (0:21-0:50)

sections.name: Phrygian Summit
sections.description: The centre shifts to an F pedal: the local key reads F minor and the tempo rises to 92.5 BPM. Opening colours of D minor-major, Gbmaj7sus and Cb/F (B/F, 0:52, 1.5 s) settle into the F-minor core: F7b5 → F → Fm7 → Fm7/Eb → Fm/C (0:54–0:58). Dbmaj7/Ab (0:59, 1.5 s) and Db7 (C#/B, 1:01) build to the measured climax at 1:02, a Db13b9 over an Ab bass, before Eb/F (1:04), Fm9/Ab and Ebm(add9) (1:05). F/Gb (1:06) grinds the Phrygian half-step, then F9/Eb (1:09) opens into F/A (1:10), which brightens the root to major. Further altered colours follow: Ebmaj13#11/F (1:12), B7#5b9 (1:14), Fmaj7#5 (A/F, 1:15–1:16), F6 and F13 (1:16–1:17). The section closes on Eb/F → Db5 → Db7 → D#aug → Dbmaj9/Eb (1:18–1:26), returning toward the Db roof.
sections.character: Full-voiced and searching at its peak, the root flickering between F minor, F major and the Gb half-step above.
sections.dynamics: Near-peak and sustained (−12.3 dBFS, 0.78–0.86); the measured climax lands at 1:02–1:05 (0.85–0.86).
sections.texture: Dense, resonant chordal texture with heavy sustain; upper-structure triads over a low F or Ab pedal.
sections.register: Widest span: F#1 to C#5 (Db5), median C#3; the melody touches its high ceiling here.
sections.emotional_beat: The summit: the longing peaks, major and minor wrestle over a single unmoving bass.
sections.imagery: Ember-red light pulsing through a stove grate while snow presses against a dark timber wall.
sections.label: Phrygian Summit (0:50-1:29)

sections.name: F Pedal Churn
sections.description: This is the loudest and brightest section (−12.2 dBFS, centroid about 1486 Hz, 4.52 attacks/s), and the median register climbs to F3 as the music fixes on F. Major and minor F alternate rapidly. Gbmaj7 with a D (1:30) and Fmaj13 with Bbmaj9/F (1:31) lead to F6/9 (Dm9/F, 1:33), Fm(add b9)/C and Fm(add4) at 1:36–1:37, then F7#9/Eb (the A-against-Ab blues clash, 1:38) and F7 (1:39). Phrygian pressure follows: Eb/F (1:40) and F/Gb (1:40), Db/F (1:41), Fm(b6b9)/Db (1:42, 1:44), and Db7 (1:42) as a pull toward Gb. The minor share peaks here (17%) with Cm (1:48), Ebsus2 and Fm7 (Ab/F, 1:51, 1.5 s). The section closes on a tight Phrygian loop of F/Gb, Gbmaj7/F and D7#9#11b13/F (1:54–1:57).
sections.character: Obsessive and churning, it circles the F root as if trying every colour of it in turn without finding rest.
sections.dynamics: Sustained forte plateau (0.81–0.87), with the intensity curve's absolute high of 0.87 at 1:55–2:00.
sections.texture: Thick, rhythmically busy chords over an F pedal; the fastest attack rate in the piece, with altered upper structures.
sections.register: Low-middle but lifted: bass from F1, median F3, melody up to G#4 (Ab4).
sections.emotional_beat: Struggle at full strength: the music grinds at its central tension, F against Gb and major against minor.
sections.imagery: A wind-driven snow squall circling a dark ridge, the low sky lit from beneath by a smoldering amber glow.
sections.label: F Pedal Churn (1:29-1:58)

sections.name: Suspended Eb Farewell
sections.description: Fmadd9 over a G (1:58) passes through Eb11 (2:00) to Ab13sus4 (2:01), the clearest dominant in the piece, which lands on Db (2:02) with Db9/Cb and Db(add9)/Ab (2:02–2:04). A last wander follows: Eb6 (2:07), Fmaj7#5 (A/F, 2:10–2:12), Ebsus2, Fsus4 (2:14), Ab6/9 (2:17), Fm7/Eb (2:17, 2:19) and F+add#9 (2:20). It then settles on a long Dbmaj7 (2:21, 2.5 s), continuing as Db(add9). Eb9 over a Db pedal (2:25) creates a Db Lydian (maj9#11) shimmer. The piece ends on Eb6/9 (labelled C4/D#, 2:28, 2.5 s) and thins to a bare Eb5 at 2:31, unresolved, a whole step above the tonic. Note density drops to 14.6 notes/s even as the local tempo rises to 98.9 BPM.
sections.character: A gentle release that refuses to close, letting the harmony hang in Lydian air rather than coming home.
sections.dynamics: Recedes from about mf (0.84 at 2:05) to a near-whisper (0.19 at 2:30); the quietest moment is at 2:28 on the Eb6/9.
sections.texture: Thinning from chordal to sustained open sonorities: long-held Dbmaj7, then bare Eb5 fifths.
sections.register: Low-middle, bass from G#1 (Ab1), median C3, melody touching C#5 (Db5) before settling.
sections.emotional_beat: Letting go without arriving: warmth returns, but the final word is a question.
sections.imagery: Last embers dimming to soft orange as pale blue twilight fills a quiet snowy clearing.
sections.label: Suspended Eb Farewell (1:58-2:35)

tempo.description: The measured tactus is 91.9 BPM. Pulse clarity is low (0.37) but steadiness is fairly high (0.81), so the beat is felt as an elastic, breathing walk rather than a metronomic one. About 4 attacks per second (eighth-note motion at this tempo) and a fast surface harmonic rhythm (chord labels change every 0.5–1 s) make it feel moderate and busy in the middle. The long pedal basses slow the perceived harmonic motion to roughly one real harmony every one to two bars. The local tempo creeps upward across the piece: 89.4 → 89.5 → 92.5 → 95.4 → 98.9 BPM. The music quietly presses forward even as the coda's dynamics recede, which gives the ending a gently restless, unsettled quality.

mode_balance.evidence: On the surface the piece reads major-leaning: 67% major, 10% minor, 8% dominant, 5% suspended, minor-weight 0.38. But many 'major' labels are slash chords whose real sonority is F-based and minor-tinged. Ab/F (G#/F, 1:51, 1.5 s) is Fm7. Eb/F (D#/F, the most-held chord in sections 2 and 3) is an F11/F9sus sonority with no third. Db/F is a first-inversion Db, i.e. Fm with a ♭6. So the bass-centred reading is F Aeolian/Phrygian, with real Fm, Fm7 and Fm9 at 0:55, 0:57, 0:58 and 1:05. The Phrygian ♭2 is constant: F/F# (1:06, 1:40, 1:55), Gbmaj7/F (labelled F#mb6M7/F, 0:33, 1:54) and Fmb6b9/C# (1:42, 1:44) all press Gb against the F bass.
