The Picardy/major-third colour flips the same root to F major: F/A at 0:12 and 1:10, Fmaj13 at 1:31, F7 at 1:39, and an F7#9 clash of A against Ab at 1:38. Augmented colours (A/F = Fmaj7#5 at 1:15 and 2:12, D#aug at 1:25) add a glassy, unresolved tint. The verdict: a major-scale collection (Db Ionian) heard from its third degree (F Phrygian), so the surface is bright while the foundation is dark.

summary.overview: Cabin Soul 5 is a dark-hued, steadily pulsing piano meditation built on a low F pedal. It circles one Aeolian engine: Db (transcribed C#) → Eb (D#) → Fm/F5, the bVI–bVII–i rise. The surface is warm and mostly major-chord, because Db and Eb dominate the held duration, but the gravity is unmistakably F minor. Barnoski's fingerprints are everywhere: Db6/9 and Dbmaj9#11 colour chords, Eb sus2 voicings over Ab, Fm7add11 and Fsus4 clouds that blur third and fourth. One luminous F/A (F major) flash at 1:11 lifts the mood, and the piece ends on an unresolved F-over-Eb sonority, suspension preferred over resolution. Emotionally it is a slow, swelling wave of introspective resolve: rooted and warm, never quite consoled.
summary.key_center: F minor (Aeolian), high confidence: the global Krumhansl estimate and four of five local estimates agree, and the bass keeps returning to F1/F2 as F5, Fm and Fm7add11. The opening section reads locally as Bb minor because it lingers on Db (relative major of Bb minor) from 0:02–0:09 and again 0:27–0:32, and starts on Bbm/Db. That is a subdominant-side colour, not a true modulation; by 0:18 the F5 pedal arrives and anchors everything. There are brief tonicizations of Db (Dbmaj9#11 at 0:49 and 1:08, where G natural is the Lydian #11 native to bVI in Aeolian) and of Ab (Abmaj9 1:10, Abmaj13 1:41). There is one parallel-major flash: F/A and Fadd9 at 1:11–1:14, which is why F major is the runner-up key. Dominant function is mostly implied rather than stated. Examples are C/Bb (C7 in third inversion) at 0:05 and 0:42, F7b9 at 0:23, G7/F → C7b9 (C/Bb/Db/G) at 1:37–1:38, and Bb/C (C9sus) at 2:18.

mood.overall: A warm, low-lit F-minor meditation that swells in patient waves toward a dense, insistent climax and then dissolves into an unresolved hush.

dynamics_arc.description: A wave of three ever-higher crests with a sharp final ebb. The first build runs from 0:00 (0.34) to 0:35 (0.74), then eases at 0:40 (0.63). A second, higher swell peaks at 1:10–1:15 (0.87), coinciding with the F major flash, and relaxes at 1:25 (0.65). From 1:30 the music climbs almost without pause through the dense 1:39–1:59 section (~0.8) to the summit at 2:04–2:10 (0.93). Then comes a steep decay: 0.82 at 2:15, 0.55 at 2:20, 0.25 at 2:25 and 0.10 at 2:30. The total dynamic range is 15.1 dB.
dynamics_arc.climax_description: The climax at ~2:04 is prepared by the chromatic dominant chain of 1:35–1:38 (Cb/F → Fdim → G7/F → C7b9). The insistent Fm repetitions of 1:54–1:57 add to the build. Last comes Db7-flavoured Db/B (2:00) → Eb/Db → Eb/C (2:01–2:03). The peak itself arrives as the harmony lands on the tonic in its most suspended form: Fm7add11 → Fsus4 → Fmadd4 → F5 → Fm (2:03–2:06). It is the bVI–bVII–i loop at full weight, cresting on a bare open fifth rather than a triumphant triad.

summary.texture_and_register: The piece is low-centred throughout: the median pitch sits around Eb3 and the bass repeatedly touches F1, giving a dark, resonant floor of open F fifths. Above it the right hand moves in pedalled broken chords and leaping melodic figures (dense leaps 0:03–0:38), rarely climbing past A4–C5. The top line never soars, which keeps the sound enclosed and warm. Voicings favour open spreads: 6/9 and maj9#11 on Db, sus2 on Eb over Ab, add11 on Fm. Density tracks the dynamic wave: attacks run 3.08/s in section 0, 4.25/s in section 1, 5.1/s at the summit, and fall to 2.77/s in the coda. The brightest timbre comes in section 2 (1773 Hz) and the darkest at the climax (1363 Hz), so the loudest music is also the most bass-heavy.
summary.emotional_narrative: The piece opens (0:00–0:18) on the warm side of the key, Db6add9 and Dbmaj7, as if lighting a fire before naming the cold. Only at 0:18 does the F5 pedal arrive, and the Db–Eb–Fm loop (0:27–0:38) reveals the minor home underneath. In the second section (0:39–1:15) the harmony reaches outward with Lydian Dbmaj9#11 and Abmaj9 colours. The striving is briefly rewarded at 1:11–1:14 with an F major (F/A) glimpse, the piece's one moment of open light. It is withdrawn immediately: from 1:15 the music hovers in Fm7add11 and sus clouds over a stubborn pedal, ambivalent between A and Ab. A chromatic dominant chain at 1:35–1:38 then gathers tension. The summit section (1:39–1:59) is the densest and darkest, hammering Fm and F5 as if insisting on the truth of the home key. The real peak lands at 2:04 on a bare, suspended tonic rather than a triumphant chord. Then everything recedes, and the last cadence (Eb/G → F/Eb, 2:22–2:24) leaves the F unresolved over its own seventh, fading into the quiet of 2:29.

imagery_cues.light: Low firelight from beneath, warm amber against deep shadow. It brightens to a cool pale-gold shaft around 1:11, thickens into flickering orange-red at the climax (2:04), and dims to a last coal glow under blue night by 2:30.
imagery_cues.motion: A slow, steady forward glide at a walking pace (~91 BPM) with a gentle eighth-note shimmer: drifting smoke, flickering flame, swaying branches. Motion intensifies into churning, swirling movement from 1:39 to 2:10, then slows to near stillness as the sound decays.
imagery_cues.scale: Intimate at the opening (a hearth, a room), widening to a landscape view at the 1:11 brightening and the 1:39–2:10 surge. It contracts back to a single glowing point in the closing seconds.
environments: a log cabin interior at dusk with a banked hearth
a snow-laden pine forest under heavy cloud
a frozen lake shore at nightfall
a mountain ridge with a brief break in the clouds
imagery_cues.atmosphere: Cold, still winter air outside, with warmth and smoke within. Heavy overcast thins once, briefly, then thickens into wind-driven turbulence at the peak before settling into a silent, frosty night.

summary.harmonic_highlights: 0:02 Db6add9: the piece begins off-tonic on bVI with a 6/9 bloom, which is why the local key reads Bb minor. 0:11–0:17: a chromatic descending smear (B/C, A/Ab, F/F#, E/F#), likely an inner line under pedal, resolving to the first F5 pedal at 0:18. 0:23 F7b9: an early dominant hint. 0:27–0:38: the core loop stated, Db/F → Db/Ab(6/9) → Ebsus2/Ab → Bbsus4 → Eb/G → F5/C (bVI–bVII–i). 0:49–0:50: Dbmaj9#11/Ab then Db/G, with Lydian G natural moved into the bass for a tritone tension. 0:57: a long Eb5 (2.5 s), the bVII suspension before Fm at 1:00. 1:11–1:14: F/A → Fadd9, a parallel-major brightening at the first crest. 1:23: F/Ab held 2.5 s, an A/Ab ambiguity (possible overtone, possibly a deliberate blues rub). 1:35–1:38: chromatic dominant approach, Cb/F → Fdim → G7/F → C7b9. 1:46: Fmaj7sus4 brings in an E natural leading-tone colour inside the tonic. 1:54–1:57: repeated Fm/Fm7/F5 tonic insistence. 2:00: Db/B, a bVI7 with augmented-sixth flavour pulling toward the climax. 2:03–2:06: the climax lands on Fm7add11 → Fsus4 → F5 → Fm. 2:18: Bb/C, a suspended dominant (C9sus) that never resolves cleanly. 2:22–2:24: Eb/G → F/Eb, a final bVII-to-tonic cadence with the b7 in the bass, an open, unresolved ending.
summary.rhythm_and_feel: The pulse is steady (90.8 BPM, steadiness 0.93), carried by continuous eighth-note motion (the 181.7 BPM alternative level) in pedalled broken-chord patterns. Pulse clarity is moderate (0.52) because sustain blurs individual attacks. The surface is busy, with chord labels changing every 0.5 s, but the functional harmonic rhythm is about one harmony per 1–2 bars, with longer holds on structural arrivals (F5 0:18 and 0:39, Eb5 0:57, F/Ab 1:23, Eb/G 2:22). Rubato is minimal; instead, energy comes from density, rising from ~3 to 5.1 attacks/s at the summit. Local tempo creeps from 89 to 92.6 BPM, giving a subtle forward lean in the second half. The coda keeps the pulse but lets chords ring instead of re-striking.
summary.relearning_tips: 1. Start with the engine, the 0:27–0:38 loop: left hand F1–C2 open fifth (or Ab/G bass as marked), right hand Db6/9 (Db–F–Ab–Bb–Eb) → Ebsus2 over Ab (Eb–F–Bb) → Eb/G → F5. Loop it at ~90 BPM in eighth notes until the pedal changes feel automatic. 2. Learn the signature colour voicings separately: Dbmaj9#11/Ab (Ab bass; Db–F–G–C), Fm7add11 (F–Ab–Bb–C–Eb) and Abmaj9/Abmaj13 (1:10, 1:41). 3. Isolate the 1:11–1:14 F/A moment, since its A natural against the minor context is the piece's emotional hinge; place it carefully and voice it slightly brighter. 4. Drill the chromatic wind-up at 1:35–1:38 (Cb/F → Fdim → G7/F → C7b9) slowly, because it leads straight into the densest passage. 5. Practise section 3 (1:39–1:59) last among the inner sections, at reduced tempo, keeping the bass F pedal clean under the thick right hand. 6. For the ending, practise the Eb/G → F/Eb release with a long held pedal and decreasing weight, letting the unresolved Eb in the bass ring. Treat the many chromatic labels at 0:11–0:17, 0:47 and 2:08–2:13 as likely inner-voice or pedal smears; reconstruct them by ear rather than trusting the transcription literally.
summary.title: Cabin Soul 5

sections.name: Kindling on Db
sections.description: The piece opens off-tonic on Bbm/Db and settles into a Db6add9 bloom (0:02, held 2 s). Eb/Db, C/Bb (an implied C7 in third inversion) and Dbmaj7 → Db/F (0:07–0:08) follow, with Eb6 at 0:10. A string of melodic leaps (0:03–0:08) sketches the first motif above. From 0:11–0:17 the labels go chromatic (B/C, A/Ab, F/F#, E/F#), probably a descending inner line smeared by the sustain pedal. That line lands on the true arrival: an F5 open fifth at 0:18 with F7sus4 and Fm7. F7b9 at 0:23 hints at the dominant. The core loop then states itself plainly: Db/F 0:27 → Db/Ab with 6 and 6/9 colours (0:28–0:32) → Ebsus2/Ab 0:33 → Bbsus4 0:35 → Eb/G 0:36 → F5/C 0:38, i.e. bVI–bVII–i.
sections.character: Tentative and warm, a voice finding its footing on the major side of the key before admitting the minor tonic.
sections.dynamics: p–mp (intensity 0.34) rising steadily to mf by 0:35 (0.74)
sections.texture: Pedalled broken-chord accompaniment with open 6/9 voicings and a leaping right-hand motif; thickens at 0:02 and again from 0:18 once the F pedal arrives.
sections.register: Low-middle: bass reaching F1, centre around F3, melody peaking near Bb4 (A#4).
sections.emotional_beat: Opening the door: the tonal home is approached obliquely through Db warmth before the F pedal grounds it at 0:18.
sections.imagery: Embers catching in a dark hearth, a low amber glow spreading slowly across rough timber as the first sparks leap upward.
sections.label: Kindling on Db (0:00-0:39)

sections.name: Lydian Swell
sections.description: An F5 pedal (0:39, held 1.5 s) and F7sus4 restart the cycle. A dominant-leaning cluster follows: C/Bb, Ebsus2/Ab, Fm and Bbsus2 (0:42–0:46), then a C/B chromatic rub at 0:47. The harmony opens to Dbmaj9#11/Ab at 0:49, whose Lydian G natural is set into tension by Db/G (0:50, 1.5 s), a tritone between bass and root. Db add9 (0:54) moves through Eb/Gb and Eb/F to a long Eb5 (0:57, 2.5 s), which resolves to Fm/Fmadd4 at 1:00. A second, richer pass follows: Fm7 1:02, C7#5sus4/Ab 1:04, Dbmaj9 1:05, Bbm9/Ab 1:07, Dbmaj9#11/Ab 1:08, Fm11/G, Abmaj9 1:10. It culminates in the surprising F/A–Fadd9 brightening at 1:11–1:14, the parallel major, right at the first intensity crest (0.87).
sections.character: Expansive and aspiring: extended Lydian colours push the harmony outward until it breaks briefly into F major light.
sections.dynamics: mf, dipping at 0:40 (0.63) and 1:00 (0.67), then cresting to f at 1:10–1:15 (0.87)
sections.texture: Denser rolling figuration (4.25 attacks/s, ~22 notes/s) with wide maj9/#11 spreads over sustained bass fifths.
sections.register: Low-centred: bass F1, median Db3 (C#3), top voice around A4; the lowest-lying section.
sections.emotional_beat: The first reach: yearning expands through Db Lydian colour and is briefly rewarded with a glimpse of major-key light.
sections.imagery: Wind pressing against a snow-covered ridge until a gap in the clouds lets a brief shaft of pale gold fall on a pine slope.
sections.label: Lydian Swell (0:39-1:15)

sections.name: Shadowed Pedal
sections.description: The F major glimpse is withdrawn at once. Fm7add11 and Fsus4 (1:15) lead to Bbm/F, the iv over the tonic pedal, then Db/Ab and Ab6add9 (1:16–1:19), Eb at 1:20 and Ebmaj7sus4/Ab. A long F/Ab (1:23, 2.5 s) carries the A-vs-Ab ambiguity: F minor with a lingering major shadow, or a bluesy rub. The loop returns in sus colours: Db/F 1:27, Eb7sus4 1:28, Db6add9 and Db6/9#11/G 1:28–1:29, Ebsus2 and Bbsus2 1:30, Fm9/Ab 1:31, Fm7add11 1:32. From 1:35 a chromatic dominant approach builds tension: B/F (Cb over F, a tritone colour) → Fdim 1:36 → G7/F 1:37 → C/Bb/Db/G (C7b9) 1:38. This launches the climax.
sections.character: Brooding and suspended, with the brightest upper-register sound of the piece (1773 Hz) floating over a stubborn F pedal before a dark chromatic wind-up.
sections.dynamics: mf held fairly level, dipping at 1:25 (0.65), then building again from 1:30 (0.71) to 1:35 (0.75)
sections.texture: Sustained sus/add11 clouds over pedal F with brighter right-hand filigree; slightly sparser attacks (3.58/s) but thick note counts (~23/s).
sections.register: Bass F1, median Eb3, upper lines reaching B4; the brightest timbre of the piece.
sections.emotional_beat: Doubt returns: the light is taken back, the harmony hovers in suspension, and a chromatic dominant chain gathers strength for the push.
sections.imagery: Dusk smoke drifting low through a forest clearing, thin cold light catching the tops of the trees while the ground sinks into shadow.
sections.label: Shadowed Pedal (1:15-1:39)

sections.name: Insistent Summit
sections.description: This is the densest passage (5.1 attacks/s, 32 notes/s). Bbm9/Ab (1:39) opens onto Dbmaj13/Ab and Ebsus2 (1:40), with Ab6add9/Abmaj13 at 1:41. Bb7sus4 and Fm11/G (1:42) drive back to F: F5 1:45, Fmaj7sus4 1:46 (E natural leading-tone colour), Fsus4 1:47. The bVI–bVII climb repeats broadly: Dbmaj9/Ab 1:47, Dbmaj7/Ab held ~2 s (1:48–1:50), Db6add9/Ab, Ebsus2/Ab 1:51, and a Gm(b6b9)/Ab cluster (effectively Eb/Ab sonority) at 1:51–1:52. The bass then hammers the tonic: Eb/F 1:53, F/Ab, and Fm–Fm7–Fm–F5 repeated 1:54–1:57. F/Eb/C, Eb/C and Db/F (1:57–1:58) pull back toward Db.
sections.character: Driven and obsessive, with the minor tonic restated again and again as if to convince itself.
sections.dynamics: f throughout (section intensity 1.0, ~0.79–0.83), the loudest sustained stretch
sections.texture: Thick, fast-moving chordal figuration with doubled bass fifths; minor (27%) and suspended (21%) chords at their highest share.
sections.register: Full span F1–C5, median Eb3; the right hand reaches its top note C5.
sections.emotional_beat: The struggle at full strength: no new light, just the home key insisted upon with growing force.
sections.imagery: A storm-driven fire roaring in a stone hearth, sparks and dark smoke churning against heavy beams.
sections.label: Insistent Summit (1:39-1:59)

sections.name: Unresolved Embers
sections.description: The section opens on the actual climax. Dbmaj7/Ab → Db/B (1:59–2:00) is effectively Db7 with Cb, an augmented-sixth-like bVI7 pull. It moves through Eb/Db and Eb/C (Cm7/Eb6 colour, 2:01–2:03) into Fm7add11 → Fsus4 → Fmadd4 → F5 → Fm (2:03–2:06), peaking at 2:04–2:05 (0.93). The cycle runs once more: Bbsus2 2:08, C/Db and Db/C/B rubs (2:08–2:10), Eb/C 2:11–2:13, Fmadd4/Fm 2:14–2:16. A dominant suspension follows: G/F 2:17, Bb/C (C9sus) 2:18, then Fm7add11. The final cadence avoids closure: Db/F 2:19 → Db 2:20 → Eb/Db/F 2:21 → Eb/G (2:22, 1.5 s) → F/Eb at 2:24. The last chord sets an F triad over its own flat seventh in the bass and is left to ring into near silence (quietest at 2:29).
sections.character: Release without resolution: after a final surge the sound dissolves on a suspended, seventh-tinged F that never fully comes home.
sections.dynamics: f at 2:04–2:10 (0.88–0.93), receding to mp by 2:20 (0.55) and fading to ppp at 2:30 (0.10)
sections.texture: Thinning attacks (2.77/s) with long pedalled resonance; chords left to decay rather than re-struck.
sections.register: Bass F1, median Eb3, top up to C5 early then settling into the middle register.
sections.emotional_beat: Aftermath: the peak breaks, the cycle is retraced quietly, and the question is left hanging in the air.
sections.imagery: The last coals of a fire glowing orange in a darkened room as cold blue night settles at the windows.
sections.label: Unresolved Embers (1:59-2:34)

tempo.description: Measured at 90.8 BPM with high steadiness (0.93). The alternative 181.7 level indicates a continuous eighth-note undercurrent, so it feels like an unhurried walking pulse with rolling motion inside it. With 3.62 attacks/s and up to 32 transcribed notes/s at the peak, the texture is busy and churning, yet the real harmonic rhythm is slow. Underneath the noisy labels, one harmony typically holds 1–2 bars (a 4/4 bar is ~2.6 s at this tempo). Examples: Db 0:27–0:32, Eb 0:33–0:38, Eb5 held 2.5 s at 0:57, F/Ab held 2.5 s at 1:23. The result reads as 'moderate': grounded and patient on top, restless underneath. There is little rubato. The local tempo even edges up from 89.2 to 92.6 BPM across the piece, a subtle forward lean into the climax and coda.

mode_balance.evidence: By held duration the chords are 63% major, 15% minor and 9% suspended, yet the minor-weight is 0.68 and the measured verdict is minor-dominant. This is the classic Aeolian paradox. The major chords are overwhelmingly Db (bVI), Eb (bVII) and Ab (bIII), the major triads native to F minor, and they keep resolving onto F5/Fm (0:18, 0:38, 0:39, 1:00, 1:45, 1:54–1:57, 2:05–2:16). Open fifths (F5) and sus chords (Fsus4, Fm7add11, Ebsus2) frequently leave the third out or blur it. That keeps the minor implied rather than declared and lends a modal, hymn-like openness. There are three counter-colours. The F/A–Fadd9 moment at 1:11–1:14 is a genuine parallel-major brightening. Fmaj7sus4 at 1:46 brings in an E natural leading-tone colour. The recurring F/Ab label (1:23, 1:33, 1:53) suggests A vs Ab ambiguity, possibly overtone noise but possibly a deliberate bluesy major/minor rub. The section-by-section minor share rises toward the climax (5% → 12% → 17% → 27%), so the piece grows darker as it intensifies.

summary.overview: "Chemiluminescence 1" is a slow-pulsed but restless F-minor piece. It is built on a low, almost hypnotic left-hand ostinato that rocks between an open F fifth (F5) and an Eb-over-C shell (labelled D#/C, effectively Cm7), with a chromatic E-natural neighbour pressing against the F. Over this pedal-like engine Karel lets the right hand leap and glow. He makes two excursions into the relative-major family: Abadd9, Dbmaj7, Bbm9 and Abmaj7/C at 0:36–0:47 and 1:09–1:17, which become the climax around 1:33–1:41. He also adds Gb-over-F Neapolitan clouds that smear the pedal before each return. The emotional core is a contained, luminous darkness: a steady 60 BPM heartbeat with sixteenth-note shimmer that swells in an arch to 1:37 and then dissolves back into the bare ostinato, never cadencing, just fading into the low register.
summary.key_center: F minor, with high certainty (Krumhansl F minor, clarity 1; every section's local estimate is F minor). The runner-up, G# (Ab) major, is the relative major. That matters because the piece's brighter episodes lean on Ab-family harmony: Abadd9 (0:36), Abmaj7/C (0:46), Dbmaj7 (0:44, 1:09, 1:33–1:35) and Bbm9 (0:43, 1:13–1:14). These are tonicizations of the relative-major colour field over iv and VI, never a full modulation, because the F/C pedal returns within seconds each time. Chromatic colour comes from three sources: E natural (the leading tone, giving Fm(maj7) at 0:25 and 0:45 and many E/F labels), Gb over F (a Neapolitan/Phrygian b2 rub at 0:57–0:58, 1:49–1:50 and 2:05–2:07), and brief B-natural tritone tints (F/B at 1:17 and 1:21, G7/F at 1:48). None of these redefine the key.

mood.overall: A dark, steadily pulsing F-minor glow that brightens through relative-major colours toward a contained climax at 1:37, then sinks back into the bare low ostinato and fades unresolved.

dynamics_arc.description: The piece follows a clear arch built in two waves. It starts from a moderate 0.44 and builds through the ostinato and leaping melody to a first crest of 0.82 at 0:45 (the Abadd9/Dbmaj7/Bbm9 bloom). It sags to 0.65 around 0:55 as the chromatic Gb/F haze gathers, then surges to a plateau of 0.83–0.89 from 1:05 to 1:30, peaking at 0.94 at 1:35–1:40. After the climax it recedes quickly to 0.58 at 1:50, holds an afterglow plateau of about 0.65–0.76 from 1:55 to 2:20, then collapses to 0.19 at 2:30 as the ostinato is left alone. The total dynamic range is 39 dB, most of it spent in the final fade.
dynamics_arc.climax_description: The climax at 1:37 is prepared by the 1:09–1:17 dwell on Dbmaj7 → Bbm9 → Bbsus, by the ostinato plateau from 1:19 to 1:28, and by the charged F7#9 (1:29) → F major (1:31) → Cm7#5 (1:32) approach. At 1:33 Dbmaj7 returns in a brighter register, and the bass descends Db (1:33) → C (1:34) → B/Bb (1:36–1:37). The peak lands on A#5, an open Bb fifth (iv), at 1:37. It then slides through C7#5sus4/G#, Bbm add4 and Eb sus over Ab to Absus2 at 1:40 and F5 at 1:41. The high point is a suspension, not a resolution. The energy is released by falling stepwise into the tonic pedal rather than by a V–i cadence.

summary.texture_and_register: The piece is built on a continuous low ostinato: sixteenth-note motion at 60 BPM on open fifths (F5, F5/C) and Eb/C (Cm7) shells, rocking around a C/F pedal with a chromatic F–E–Eb inner line. This keeps the median pitch low (D#3 overall) and the density very high (4.42 attacks/s, up to 21 transcribed notes/s in Section 2). Above it, the right hand alternates between wide-leaping single lines (0:08–0:37) and thick extended voicings such as Abadd9, Bbm9, Dbmaj7, Dbmaj13 and sus2/sus4 stacks (0:36–0:47, 1:09–1:17, 1:33–1:40). The overall range runs G#1 to C5, so the piece never goes very high; brightness comes from voicing and spectrum (centroid rising from ~1400 Hz to ~2570 Hz in Sections 2–3) rather than register. Section 1 sits highest (median C4), Section 3 is the most open and resonant, and Section 5 strips everything back to the bass skeleton between C2 and F3.
summary.emotional_narrative: From 0:00 to 0:05 a chromatic upward swirl ignites the piece and lands on a deep F at 0:05, and the ostinato engine begins: F5 rocking against Cm7 over a C pedal, with E natural pressing in. Through 0:08–0:35 a restless right hand leaps above it, and the minor third (Fm, Fm(maj7)) gradually comes into focus as the intensity builds. At 0:36 the light turns warm for the first time: Abadd9, Dbmaj7, Bbm9 and Abmaj7/C bloom in the upper-middle register, a glimpse of the relative major. The F pedal pulls it back by 0:47, and a C-suspended dominant (0:53) and F11 (0:55) dissolve into a Gb-over-F chromatic haze (0:56–1:01). From 1:01 the piece burns at full strength, with the ostinato at its loudest and a longer dwell on Dbmaj7 → Bbm9 → Bbsus (1:09–1:17). It drives through F7#9 and Cm7#5 toward the summit. The climax at 1:37 is a held suspension on Bb over a stepwise falling bass (Db–C–Bb–Ab–F), a bittersweet exhale rather than a victory. After 1:41 the energy recedes into Neapolitan clouds (1:49) and an afterglow ostinato (1:53–2:15) that circles without climbing. From 2:15 only the bare bass pattern remains, softer and softer, and the piece ends on an unresolved Ab-over-F shell, its light fading by 2:30.

imagery_cues.light: Self-generated light from below in an otherwise dark space. It starts as a faint pulsing violet, swells to a warm amber-gold radiance through 1:01–1:40, cools back to violet, and gutters out to darkness by 2:30.
imagery_cues.motion: Slow, steady drift locked to a 60 BPM heartbeat, with fine shimmering micro-motion (the sixteenth-note surface) everywhere. Gentle upward rising during the blooms, a slow downward settling after 1:37, and a near-still, pulsing hold at the end.
imagery_cues.scale: Intimate at the start, a single glowing source in the dark. It expands to fill a whole chamber or basin at 1:01–1:40, then contracts back to a single dimming point by the fade.
environments: a lightless underground pool with glowing water
a deep ocean floor at night lit by bioluminescent drift
a dark laboratory glass vessel pulsing with reactive light
a nocturnal cave grotto with luminous mineral seams
imagery_cues.atmosphere: Still, cool, humid darkness with a faint haze that catches and diffuses the glow; windless and enclosed, with the pulse the only movement.

chord_vocabulary: Cm7 shell / Eb over C (labelled D#/C)
summary.harmonic_highlights: 0:00–0:05: a rising chromatic chain (E/F → A#/G# → A/G#/F# → B/G#/F# → C/B/G#) acts as an upbeat that lands on the deep F5 at 0:05. 0:05 onward: the tonic pedal ostinato F5 ↔ Eb/C (Cm7) with an F–E–Eb inner descent, the harmonic DNA of the piece and still present alone at 2:15–2:24. 0:25 and 0:45: Fm(maj7), the harmonic-minor leading tone as colour rather than a cadence. 0:36–0:46: Abadd9 → Db → Bbm9 → Dbmaj7 → Abmaj7/C, the relative-major bloom built from iv, VI and III extensions. 0:53–0:55: C5 / Cmaj7sus4 → F11, a dominant that suspends instead of resolving. 0:56–1:01, 1:49–1:50 and 2:05–2:07: Gb over F Neapolitan/Phrygian smears over the pedal, signalling each transition. 1:09–1:17: the extended dwell Dbmaj7 → C#7/B → Dbmaj13/C → Bbm9 → Bbsus2 → Bb7sus4 → Bb5. 1:17 and 1:21: F/B tritone tints. 1:29: F7#9 (Ab against A), then a fleeting F major at 1:31, a Picardy flicker that is immediately withdrawn. 1:33–1:41: the climax line Dbmaj7 → C → Bb5 (1:37) → Absus2 → F5, a stepwise descending bass cushioned in suspensions. 1:48: G7 over F (V/V over the pedal). 2:24: the ending on Ab over F with a cluster, with no cadence.
summary.rhythm_and_feel: The pulse is a metronomic 60 BPM (steadiness 0.99) with essentially no rubato. The piece's rhythmic identity is a continuous four-per-beat (sixteenth-note) ostinato, which also produces the 120 BPM secondary reading. Harmonic rhythm in the ostinato is fast and regular, changing chord on roughly every beat (F5 → Cm7 → F5/C). In the bloom passages it slows into one- to two-beat sustained extended chords (Bbm9, Dbmaj7, sus stacks), so the music breathes even though the surface never stops. The right-hand leaps from 0:08 to 0:37 fall roughly every one to three seconds, cutting across the steady grid. The feel is trance-like and propulsive yet unhurried, a motor running at resting heart rate.
summary.relearning_tips: 1. Rebuild the left-hand ostinato first, since it carries most of the piece: F2–C3 fifth alternating with a C–Eb–G–Bb (Cm7) shell, with the inner line F → E → Eb. Use a metronome at 60 and play four even notes per click until it runs on autopilot; Section 5 (2:15–2:24) is the cleanest reference for it. 2. Learn the opening chromatic rise (0:00–0:05) as one gesture that lands squarely on the 0:05 downbeat. 3. Isolate the bloom chain Abadd9 → Db → Bbm9 → Dbmaj7 → Abmaj7/C (0:36–0:46). Voice the Bbm9 with Db–F–Ab–C on top, the Dbmaj7 with F–Ab–C on top, and keep common tones (Ab, C, F) held between chords. 4. Practise the climax descent separately: Dbmaj7 (1:33) → C bass → Bb5 (1:37) → Absus2 (1:40) → F5 (1:41). Let the sus2/sus4 voicings ring and voice-lead the top line downward. 5. Learn the Gb-over-F transition clusters (0:57, 1:49, 2:05) as a fixed hand shape (Gb–Bb–Db over an F pedal) that signals 'return coming'. 6. Then assemble the piece in order, shaping the dynamics in the two waves (crest at 0:45, summit at 1:37). Treat the final bars as the ostinato alone, fading. Labels such as C#maj7#9#11/C or D#M#5add9/B are likely overtone noise; trust the underlying Db, Bb and Gb shapes over the exotic extensions.
summary.title: Chemiluminescence 1

sections.name: Ignition and Ostinato
sections.description: The piece opens with a rising chromatic swirl, 0:00–0:04: E/F → A#/G# → G#/F → A/G#/F# → B/G#/F# → C/B/G#. It climbs semitone by semitone like a fuse burning upward and lands on a deep bass impact at 0:05 (F5). From there the engine starts: F5 (0:05) → D#/C (0:06) → F5/C (0:07) → D#/C (0:08) → F5 (0:09). This is an open-fifth i alternating with an Eb-over-C (Cm7) shell, with E/F neighbours (0:13, 0:17) and Cdim/F# flickers (0:12, 0:18) chromatically rubbing the pedal. From 0:08 the right hand enters with a run of wide melodic leaps (detected at 0:08, 0:12, 0:13, 0:17, 0:18, 0:20, 0:22, 0:26, 0:29–0:35), and the third finally colours in. Explicit Fm appears from 0:27, Fm(maj7) at 0:25, and Ab6 (G#6) at 0:22 and 0:26. A dense C#maj7#9#11/C at 0:21 hints at the Db colour to come.
sections.character: An insistent, low-lit machine starting up, with a restless leaping line sparking above a pedal that refuses to move.
sections.dynamics: Starts moderate (intensity 0.44) and builds steadily to 0.75 by 0:25–0:30, holding around -14.6 dBFS; a strong accent on the 0:05 bass hit.
sections.texture: Busy sixteenth-note left-hand ostinato on open fifths and Cm7 shells, with sparse, wide-leaping right-hand melody above; dense (14 notes/s).
sections.register: Low to middle: bass anchored on F2/C2 down to A1, median around C3, melody reaching up to G#4.
sections.emotional_beat: Ignition: a spark climbs chromatically and catches, and the low engine begins to pulse.
sections.imagery: A dark vessel of liquid where a thin thread of light rises from the bottom and blooms into a slow, rhythmic pulsing glow along the glass.
sections.label: Ignition and Ostinato (0:00-0:36)

sections.name: Relative-Major Bloom
sections.description: The texture lifts by nearly an octave (median C4) and the harmony turns to the Ab family: G#Madd9 (Abadd9) at 0:36, C#5 (Db) at 0:37 and C#sus2/4 at 0:38. Next come Fm with b6/maj7 colour at 0:39, an Fm add4 at 0:42, then A#m7 → A#m9 (Bbm9, iv9) at 0:43, C#maj7 (Dbmaj7, VImaj7) at 0:44 and G#maj7/C (Abmaj7/C, IIImaj7) at 0:46. That is a warm iv–VI–III chain of extended voicings. At 0:47 the ostinato reasserts itself: Fm, Fm/C, D#/C, Fm. Then it drives to the dominant, C/D# → CM7sus4 (0:53) → C5 (0:54), and an F11 at 0:55 suspends rather than resolves. From 0:56 to 1:01 a chromatic cloud gathers (A#/A/G#/B, G#/F/F#, F/F#, F#/F, E/C, D#M#5add9/B): the Gb-over-F Neapolitan smear that blurs the pedal before the next wave.
sections.character: The first warmth: suspended major-seventh and ninth colours open the space before chromatic haze pulls it back down.
sections.dynamics: Peaks at 0.82 around 0:45, then recedes to 0.65 by 0:55 as the chromatic cloud gathers; about -13.1 dBFS.
sections.texture: Extended chordal voicings (add9, m9, maj7) layered over the continuing pulse, thinning into chromatic semitone clusters at the end.
sections.register: Middle, the highest-centred section: median C4, range A#1 to C#5, melody brushing C5–C#5.
sections.emotional_beat: Hope glimpsed: the light briefly turns warm before chromatic shadow seeps back in.
sections.imagery: The glow spreads upward through a dark chamber, turning from cold violet to soft amber, then clouds over as faint semitone ripples blur its edges.
sections.label: Relative-Major Bloom (0:36-1:01)

sections.name: Full Radiance
sections.description: This is the loudest and brightest sustained passage (-11.2 dBFS, centroid ~2539 Hz, intensity 1.0). It restarts the ostinato at full strength: F5/Fm7 (1:01) → C/D# → G#6 (Ab6, i.e. Fm7 colour) → F5/C → D#/C → F/E (1:05). At 1:09 the bloom returns, larger than before: Fmb6M7/C# → C#maj7 (Dbmaj7) → C#7/B → C#maj13/C (1:12) → A#m9 (1:13–1:14) → A#sus2 → G#6add9 → A#7sus4 → A#5 (1:15–1:17). That is a long dwell on Bb-minor-ninth and Bb-suspended colour (iv) over a descending bass Db–C–Bb. At 1:17 the harmony returns to the F pedal via a tritone tint (F/B) and runs the ostinato from 1:19 to 1:28 with Fm7/C, F/B/A# and F/E rubs. The section ends charged: F7#9 at 1:29 (Ab against A), a fleeting F major at 1:31, then Cm7#5 at 1:32 leaning into the climax.
sections.character: Sustained at full glow, the iv9 suspensions are held long enough to ache while the pedal keeps throbbing beneath.
sections.dynamics: Sustained forte-equivalent plateau, intensity 0.83–0.89, with a dip to 0.83 at 1:25 and a re-surge to 0.88 at 1:30 heading into the climax.
sections.texture: The densest texture (21 notes/s): full sixteenth ostinato plus thick extended right-hand chords; bright and resonant.
sections.register: Low to middle with a wide span: bass down to A#1, median C3, upper voices to G#4.
sections.emotional_beat: Full emission: the reaction is at its strongest and the pulse carries the warmth and the tension together.
sections.imagery: An entire dark basin lit from within, its surface pulsing in time and throwing rippling violet-gold light across wet stone walls.
sections.label: Full Radiance (1:01-1:33)

sections.name: Summit and Descent
sections.description: The climax arrives at 1:37 by way of a descending stepwise bass line under major-seventh colour: C#maj7 (Dbmaj7, 1:33–1:35) → G#/C and Cmb6b9/C# (1:34) → G#/B → A#5 (Bb, 1:37, the peak) → C7#5sus4/G# → A#madd4 → D#sus2/4 over G# → G#sus2 (1:40) → F5 (1:41). The bass falls roughly Db–C–Bb–Ab–F, VI to i, cushioned entirely in suspensions, the most Barnoski-like gesture in the piece. From 1:41 to 1:46 the ostinato resumes (F5, C/D#/F, G#6, F5/C, D#/C). A G7 over F at 1:48 adds a V/V tint with B natural against the pedal. C#Madd9 at 1:49 and then F#/F, F#/F and E/F/C (1:49–1:50) bring back the Gb Neapolitan haze, ending on a cloudy D#M#5add9 at 1:52.
sections.character: The arrival at the top is not triumphant but a held, suspended exhale sliding down a stepwise bass into the pedal.
sections.dynamics: Climax at 1:37 (0.94), then a fast recession to 0.58 by 1:50; about -14.8 dBFS on average because of the drop.
sections.texture: Fewer attacks (3.95/s) but sustained, open sus2/sus4 and maj7 voicings that let the resonance ring; it thins into chromatic semitone clusters.
sections.register: Middle-centred, median F3: bass from A1, top voices to C5, the bright upper partials giving the highest centroid of the full sections.
sections.emotional_beat: Peak and release: the brightest point resolves not by cadence but by sinking, step by step, back into the dark pulse.
sections.imagery: A flare of glow at its fullest radius, its colour softening to rose-amber as it slowly drops through layered translucent water toward the floor.
sections.label: Summit and Descent (1:33-1:53)

sections.name: Afterglow Ostinato
sections.description: The pedal engine returns, darker and lower-centred (median A#3, centroid ~1583 Hz): F7#9/C → F5/C (1:53) → C/D# → F5 → D#/C → F/D#/E → F/F# (1:57) → G#6 → Fm (1:59) → D#/C → Cm (2:00, a minor v). It is the same chromatic F–E–Eb shading above a C pedal. A short chromatic detour at 2:01–2:08 heads away from the pedal through C/A, G#Maddb9, B/A#, G7b9#9/D, F#/F (2:05–2:07, the Neapolitan rub again), F#M7sus4/B and C/E/F. It settles on D#5/A# → A#sus4 (Bbsus4, iv, 2:08) and drops back to F5/C. The ostinato then runs undisturbed from 2:09 to 2:13 (F5/C, D#/C, Emb6M7/C, F/E, F5), touching G#M (Ab) at 2:14 as a last glint of the relative major.
sections.character: A cooling, steady circling, the reaction still alive but no longer reaching upward, with shadowy chromatic eddies.
sections.dynamics: A moderate plateau around 0.65–0.76 (small swell at 2:00), -13 dBFS, gradually flattening.
sections.texture: Ostinato-dominant with lighter right-hand activity (14.8 notes/s); chromatic clusters at 2:03–2:07 briefly thicken it.
sections.register: Low-middle: C2 to C5, median A#3; the melody steps back from the upper register.
sections.emotional_beat: Afterglow: the same pattern repeats, but the energy is now residual, a memory of the bloom.
sections.imagery: The glow settling into a slow tidal pulse at the bottom of a dark pool, faint chromatic shimmers drifting off its edges like dissolving trails.
sections.label: Afterglow Ostinato (1:53-2:15)

sections.name: Fading Embers
sections.description: Everything above the ostinato falls away. At -35.4 dBFS, with only 5.3 notes/s, the left-hand pattern is heard alone in the low register: F5/C (2:15) → D#/C → E/F → F5 → C/D# → D#/F → F5/C (2:19) → D#/C → F/E/D# → F5/C → D#/C → F/D#. It is the bare F–E–Eb chromatic descent over C, the skeleton the whole piece was built on. At 2:24 a final G#/F (Ab over F, an Fm-colour shell) and an A#/B/G# cluster leave it hanging without a cadence. The sound decays to its quietest point at 2:30. The high spectral centroid (~2978 Hz) at this soft level likely reflects room tone and decay rather than new upper material.
sections.character: The engine runs down alone in the dark, unresolved, slowly losing its light.
sections.dynamics: A sudden drop to pp (intensity 0.45 at 2:25, then 0.19 at 2:30), fading to silence by 2:35.
sections.texture: Bare single-hand ostinato: open fifths and two- to three-note shells, with no melody.
sections.register: Low only: C2 to F3, median F2.
sections.emotional_beat: Extinction: the reaction exhausts itself and the pulse persists faintly until the light is gone.
sections.imagery: A last faint pulse of violet at the bottom of a black pool, each beat dimmer, until only the dark water remains.
sections.label: Fading Embers (2:15-2:35)

tempo.description: The measured tactus is a rock-steady 60.1 BPM (steadiness 0.99, pulse clarity 0.79), and the harmonic oscillation moves roughly once per beat or every two beats (F5 → D#/C → F5/C). That makes the large-scale pulse feel slow, like a resting heartbeat. Underneath, though, the attack rate of 4.42 per second means about four notes per beat: a continuous sixteenth-note undercurrent. That is why the alternative metrical level of 120 BPM also registers. The result is a paradox of slow motion with fast surface: unhurried and unrubato'd at the beat level, yet shimmering and busy at the note level. There is no measurable tempo drift across sections (60.0–60.4), so all growth comes from register, density and dynamics, not from pushing the tempo.

mode_balance.evidence: The raw chord-quality share reads 60% major, but this is a transcription artefact. The ostinato is mostly open fifths (F5, F5/C) and slash shells (D#/C, C/D#) that the labeller files as 'major', and power fifths carry no third. Pitch-class weighting gives a minor-weight of 0.68 and a minor-dominant verdict, and the explicit thirds are Ab: Fm at 0:27, 0:29, 0:31, 0:35, 0:47 and 0:49, plus Fm7 at 1:01, 1:20 and 1:25. Several features confirm harmonic minor rather than a modal reading. The E natural (Fm/ma7 at 0:25 and 0:45, frequent E/F) is the raised leading tone. The dominant appears as C5 / CM7sus4 at 0:53–0:54. Cm and Cm7#5 at 2:00 and 1:32 give a natural-minor v. The bright episodes borrow from the relative major (Db, Ab, Bbm9) rather than shifting the mode. The Gb/F rubs add a Phrygian/Neapolitan shade, but they are passing colour, which is why no modal colour was detected. The F7#9 at 1:29 and 1:53 is a blues-tinged major/minor-third clash over the pedal (Ab against A), not a shift to major.

summary.overview: "Rolling 2" is a slow, warmly consonant G-major meditation built from two broad tidal swells and a long ebb. Its harmonic world is almost entirely diatonic: I, IV and V (81% major by held duration), voiced with Barnoski's open add9, 6/9, maj9 and maj13 colours, a Lydian #11 on the IV chord, and a ii chord (Am7–Am13) that darkens the quieter passages. The 'rolling' quality comes from a slow pendulum between G and C under a sustain pedal: low attack rate (~2/s), many notes per onset, chords spread upward from a deep bass. The emotional core is grateful, unhurried contentment that swells to two full-voiced peaks (0:58 and 1:55) and then lets go. It ends not on a firm cadence but on a hovering G6add9 cloud.
summary.key_center: G major, with high confidence (Krumhansl clarity 1; every section except one estimates G major locally). The tonic is set from the first seconds (GM at 0:02–0:12) and returned to at every phrase end (0:38, 0:53, 1:09, 1:28, 1:40, 2:03, 2:19, 2:55, 3:06). The runner-up D major is not a real modulation. It reflects how much time the music spends on V (D, Dmaj7, D7, D9) and, in Section 4 (2:19–2:45), an A pedal under D/A, D9/A and C6/9#11/A. That pedal makes the local estimate tip to D major while the progression is really an Am7–D9 (ii–V) oscillation in G. There are no secondary dominants or real tonicizations. The only out-of-key colours are the Lydian F# on C chords (C6/9#11 at 0:46, 1:03, 1:58, 2:14), which is still diatonic to G, and a probably spurious 'Daug' and 'Gm69/D' in the coda (2:50, 2:59), most likely passing-tone or overtone noise.

mood.overall: Warm, grateful contentment that swells twice into full-hearted fullness and then settles into a quiet, slightly wistful stillness without fully closing.

dynamics_arc.description:
Two tidal waves and a long ebb, matching the measured 'falling' overall shape and 22.3 dB range.
- First rise (0:00–1:00): intensity climbs from about 0.3 to 0.88 over a minute of I–IV pendulum.
- First fall (1:05–1:35): recedes to 0.30 in the shaded Am interlude.
- Second rise (1:40–2:15): surges quickly from 0.38 at 1:40 to 0.85 at 1:55, then holds a high plateau (0.70–0.79) until about 2:15.
- Long decay (2:20–3:05): 0.60 → 0.44 → 0.38 → a small swell to 0.44 at 2:55 when G returns, then fades to 0.15 at 3:05.
The second wave is louder on average but more of a sustained plateau; the first contains the single loudest moment.
dynamics_arc.climax_description: The loudest point is at about 0:58–1:00 (intensity 0.88). It is prepared by 45 seconds of gradually widening I–IV swings and by the first move to V at 0:42 (Gmaj9/D → D major). The first D–C(Lydian)–Am13–G descent (0:43–0:53) lands on a 3.5-second G, and the climax arrives as the cycle restarts: Gadd9 (0:57) and a G major-7 voicing (0:58) flowing into D/Dmaj7 (0:59–1:02). The bass goes down to G1, the deepest note in the piece, and note density more than doubles while attacks stay around 2/s. The peak is therefore a swell of resonance and depth, not of speed. A second, broader high point follows at 1:55 (0.85), where the D7 at 1:57 adds the piece's only real dominant tension before resolving onto C6/9#11.

summary.texture_and_register:
Throughout, the texture is pedalled, rolled chordal piano. A deep bass note (often a G or C re-struck about every eight beats, or a pedal under shifting harmony) supports wide add9/6/9/maj9/maj13 voicings that are spread upward and let ring. The melody emerges from the top voice, often by leaps. The ratio of notes to attacks shows how texture changes while the rate of attacks barely does:
- Peak sections (1 and 3): about 36–38 notes/s against about 2 attacks/s, i.e. thick, many-voiced onsets.
- Quiet sections (2, 4, 5): 12–23 notes/s, more transparent.
Register spans G1–A5 with a median of A3, so the piece lives in the warm low-middle of the instrument. The loud sections sit lower: Section 3 has a median of F#3, and Section 1 reaches the deepest note, G1. The quiet sections are both softer and duller in timbre (centroids of 615–669 Hz in Sections 2 and 4, against about 1100–1280 Hz in Sections 0, 1 and 3), so 'dark' passages are muted rather than minor. The coda thins out until the final sonority is a rootless A–B–D cluster in the middle register.
summary.emotional_narrative: The piece opens (0:00–0:42) with a gentle sway between G and C, the add9 and 6 colours making each chord feel open and warm, and each swing a little fuller. At 0:42 the harmony reaches D for the first time and the music opens up. A falling D–C(Lydian)–Am–G cadence carries it to the full, deep-voiced peak at about 0:58, where the bass touches G1. From 1:14 the warmth turns inward: Am7, Am11 and Am13 chords and long, unresolved C major-9 and major-13 colours create a hushed, shaded reflection, the darkest-toned passage, which ends holding its breath on IV at 1:50. The second swell answers at 1:50 with more weight than the first. G, D and an actual D7 at 1:57 and 2:13 push forward, but each time the dominant falls lovingly onto C rather than straight home: affirmation through suspension rather than arrival. From 2:19 the energy drains while the surface ripples. The bass drifts onto A under Am7–D9 circles, so the ground feels less certain even as the colours stay warm. The coda at 2:45 passes through a bittersweet Bm shadow, settles plagally from C to G at 2:55, and then dissolves. The final sound at 3:07 is an A–B–D cluster, a G add9 without its root, so home is reached in feeling but left gently open.

imagery_cues.light: Low, warm side-light that brightens to full gold at the two swells (0:58, 1:55), dims to cool, filtered shade in the Am interlude (1:14–1:50), and fades through amber into lavender twilight in the coda.
imagery_cues.motion: Slow, continuous gliding with a gentle rise and fall about every eight seconds, like riding long swells. The motion lifts and widens into the peaks, slows almost to stillness in the interlude, ripples lightly in the ebb (2:19–2:45), and comes to a near-motionless drift at the end.
imagery_cues.scale: It begins human-scale and close, expands to vast, open vistas at the two climaxes (0:58 and 1:55–2:15), draws back to an intimate, sheltered scale in the interlude, and ends intimate and still as the landscape dissolves into haze.
environments: rolling grassland hills at late afternoon
a wide coastal bay with long, slow swells
a quiet lake shore at dusk
a shaded hollow at the edge of a wheat field
an open valley seen from a high ridge at sunset
imagery_cues.atmosphere: Mild, still, slightly humid air with a soft haze; occasional passing cloud-shade in the middle, and a cool evening mist rising at the close.

summary.harmonic_highlights:
- 0:02–0:41: an I–IV pendulum (G ↔ C) with frequent G pedal under C (CM/G 0:13, C6add9/G 0:15, Cadd9/G 0:24): the 'rolling' engine of the piece.
- 0:42–0:43: first arrival on V (Gmaj9/D → D), a suspension-like moment in which the G-major-9 colour sits over D before D major sounds clean.
- 0:46, 1:03, 1:58, 2:14: C6/9#11, the Lydian raised 11th (F#) on IV. Barnoski's modal colour, still diatonic to G.
- 0:49 and 1:05–1:06: Am13/C and Am9/C → Am13/G, the ii chord sliding in as a softer substitute for IV in a D–C–Am–G descending cadence.
- 1:15–1:25: the longest stretch of ii (Am7/Am11/Am13), with an Esus/A → D6add9/A suspension (1:25–1:26) resolving to Gmaj13 (1:27).
- 1:31–1:50: an extended dwelling on IV (Cmaj13, C6add9, Cmaj9/G), which ends the interlude unresolved on IV and makes the G at 1:50 feel like a renewed arrival.
- 1:57 and 2:13–2:14: D7, the only real dominant-seventh sound, resolving deceptively to C6/9#11 (V7–IV, a retrogression) instead of to G. This is the 'suspension over resolution' signature.
- 2:26–2:37: A pedal under D/A, D9/A, Am7, C6/9#11/A and D7add6/A, a ii–V circling that tips the local key estimate toward D.
- 2:45–2:49: a Bm/iii shadow (B5/F#, Bm/D) opening the coda.
- 2:51–2:55: plagal C → G homecoming.
- 3:06–3:07: final G6add9 → D5/A → A–B–D cluster, a rootless add9 ending left ringing rather than closed.
summary.rhythm_and_feel: The feel is a slow 4 at about 59 BPM, with eighth-note rolling at about 117 giving the surface its motion. Pulse clarity is low (0.38) because chords are rolled and pedalled rather than struck on the beat, but steadiness is high (0.89), so the rubato is a gentle stretching inside an even underlying pace. Harmonic rhythm is broad, roughly one chord every 4–8 beats with tonic holds of up to 10 beats. Deep bass re-attacks about every eight beats (0:04, 0:13, 0:21, 0:32) shape the music into eight-beat breath-waves. Busier but softer rippling appears in Section 4 (2.88 attacks/s), and the piece thins to its sparsest rhythm (1.74/s) in the coda. Local tempo relaxes slightly at the ends (56.4 and 56.6 BPM).
summary.relearning_tips:
1. Start with the engine, the G ↔ C pendulum of 0:00–0:42. In the left hand, use a low G (G1/G2) with a fifth or octave, and keep a G bass under C often (C/G). In the right hand, voice Gadd9 as B–D–A or D–G–A–B, and C as E–G–D (add9) or E–A–D (6/9). Roll each chord upward at an eighth-note pace (~117) under the pedal.
2. Learn the cadence that defines the climaxes: Gmaj9/D → D → C6/9#11 → Am13 (or Am9/C) → Cmaj13#11/G → G, as at 0:42–0:53 and 0:59–1:09. Put the F# on top of or inside the C chord so the Lydian colour sings.
3. Learn Section 3's variant, G → D → D7 → C6/9#11 → G (1:50–2:10, repeated 2:10–2:18). Let the C natural of D7 resolve down to B inside the Cmaj7/C6/9 voicing rather than to G.
4. Add the quiet sections. In the interlude (1:14–1:50), practise Am7 → Am11 → Am13 voicings and the long Cmaj9/Cmaj13 holds. In the ebb (2:19–2:45), hold a low A while alternating D/A, D9 and Am7.
5. Finish with the coda (2:45–3:09): Bm/D → Gmaj7 → C → G, then the dissolving add9 ending. Release the bass and let the final A–B–D ring.
Practice order: Section 0 → 1 → 3 (shared material), then 2 → 4 → 5. Shape dynamics in long eight-beat waves. Use half-pedalling at the peaks so the dense maj9/13 voicings stay clear rather than muddy.
summary.title: Rolling 2

sections.name: Opening Pendulum
sections.description: After a hazy pickup (B/A at 0:00), the tonic is set as a long G major (0:02–0:12) coloured by G6 and a G major-7 voicing (the 'Bmb6M7/G' labels at 0:04, 0:20 and 0:27–0:28), with a deep bass strike at 0:04. The phrase rocks to IV: CM/G and Cadd9 at 0:13, then C6add9/G at 0:15, often over a G pedal in the bass, back to Gadd9/G at 0:17–0:20, then Cmaj13 and Cadd9 at 0:21–0:24. It repeats the swing more fully: G at 0:26–0:29, C6/C at 0:30–0:36, a G/B passing bass at 0:37, landing on G (0:38, 3 s) and G6 at 0:41. Melodic leaps cluster at 0:06–0:18 and 0:25–0:33: the right hand climbs through the add9/6 tones (A, E) above a middle-register G3 centre. Bass re-strikes roughly every eight beats (0:13, 0:21, 0:32, 0:34) mark the phrase waves.
sections.character: A gentle, rocking I–IV pendulum that grows a little fuller with each swing.
sections.dynamics: p to mp, building steadily: intensity 0.34 at 0:00, 0.49 by 0:20, 0.63 at 0:30, 0.65 at 0:40; the section average is -21.4 dBFS.
sections.texture: Pedalled broken chords: a low bass note re-struck every phrase, open add9/6 chord tones rolled upward, and a melodic line emerging from the top voice with frequent leaps.
sections.register: Low-middle: bass from C2 to G2, harmony centred around G3, top voice reaching B4.
sections.emotional_beat: Arrival and settling in: the home key and the I–IV sway are laid out like a first breath.
sections.imagery: Long low swells of grassland rolling under a slow breeze in mid-afternoon light, each wave a little taller than the last.
sections.label: Opening Pendulum (0:00-0:42)

sections.name: First Swell
sections.description: The harmony steps up to V for the first time: Gmaj9/D at 0:42 into a full D major (0:43, 2.5 s). It then descends through IV with its Lydian colour (C6/9#11 at 0:46, C at 0:47, Cadd9 at 0:48), the ii chord as a soft substitute (Am13/C at 0:49), and Cmaj13#11/G at 0:51 back to a long G (0:53, 3.5 s). The same D–C–Am–G descent repeats at greater weight. This time Gadd9 (0:57) and a G major-7 voicing reach the peak at 0:58–1:00, then D and Dmaj7 (0:59–1:02), C6/9#11 and C (1:03–1:05), Am9/C and Am13/G (1:05–1:06), Cmaj13#11/G and G (1:07–1:12). It closes on Dsus4/G to Gadd9 (1:12–1:13). The bass drops to G1, the lowest note of the piece, and note density more than doubles (36 notes/s against about 2 attacks/s): each onset is a wide, many-voiced rolled chord.
sections.character: The music opens its chest: a falling V–IV–ii–I cadence sung with full, deep-voiced chords.
sections.dynamics: mf to f: intensity rises from 0.78 at 0:45 to the piece's loudest point at 0:58–1:00 (0.88), then recedes to 0.51 by 1:10; the section average is -15.6 dBFS.
sections.texture: Dense pedalled sonorities: deep bass octaves and fifths, rolled maj9/maj13 voicings in the middle, and the melody riding on top.
sections.register: Widest low end of the piece: bass down to G1, median around B3, top reaching D5.
sections.emotional_beat: The first fullness of feeling: the welcome becomes an embrace, then gently lets go.
sections.imagery: Sunlight breaking fully across a wide valley as a broad hill-swell crests, the whole landscape glowing gold for a moment before the light softens.
sections.label: First Swell (0:42-1:14)

sections.name: Shaded Interlude
sections.description: Coming down from the peak, Gadd9/D (1:14) gives way to the piece's longest stretch of minor colour: Am11, Am7 and Am13 at 1:15–1:17. These pass through a Lydian IV (labelled CM7b5/F# at 1:18, a C major-7 with F# in the bass; Cmaj13#11/G at 1:19) into Gadd9 (1:19–1:22). The ii chord returns (Am9, Am7, Am13 at 1:23–1:25), with an Esus/A and D6add9/A suspension (1:25–1:26) leading to Gmaj13/G6/G (1:27–1:30). From 1:31 the music rests on IV more than anywhere else: Cmaj13, C, C6add9 and Cadd9 (1:31–1:39), a brief G (1:40–1:42), a Dsus touch (1:43), then a long, unresolved C6add9 / Cmaj13 / Cmaj9/G (1:43–1:50). Brightness falls to about 615 Hz, the darkest of the piece. Attacks rise slightly (2.47/s) but at low dynamics, so it reads as soft, murmuring motion rather than energy.
sections.character: An inward, hushed reflection where the ii chord and lingering IV colours replace the earlier glow with soft shade.
sections.dynamics: p, near-steady: intensity 0.51 at 1:20 sinks to 0.30 at 1:30–1:35, then begins to stir (0.38 at 1:40, 0.43 at 1:45); the section average is -23.8 dBFS.
sections.texture: Lighter, more transparent arpeggiation; soft bass under rolled Am7/Am13 and Cmaj9/13 voicings, with a few high top notes reaching toward B5.
sections.register: Middle, darker in tone: bass around C2–G2, median B3, occasional high points near B5, overall timbre muted.
sections.emotional_beat: Looking inward after the first embrace; a quiet memory with a trace of longing, which ends hovering on IV as if holding its breath.
sections.imagery: A shaded hollow at the edge of a field under passing cloud, cool green light, grasses barely moving.
sections.label: Shaded Interlude (1:14-1:50)

sections.name: Second Swell
sections.description: The IV that closed Section 2 opens onto a strong G (1:50–1:53) with Gadd9 and Gmaj9 (1:54). The harmony then drives to V with a real dominant edge for the first time: D (1:54), Gmaj9#11/D and Gmaj9/D over a D bass (1:55–1:56), D and D7 (1:56–1:57). The D7 resolves not to G but to the Lydian IV: C6/9#11 (1:58), Em9#5/C (effectively Cmaj7), and Cadd9/C6add9/C (1:59–2:02), before G6 and G return (2:02–2:10). The cycle repeats almost exactly: Gmaj9/D (2:10), D (2:11), Gmaj9 (2:12), D7 (2:13–2:14), C6/9#11 (2:14), then C, Cadd9, C6add9 and Cmaj9 (2:15–2:18). The lowest attack rate of the piece (1.79/s), the highest note density (37.8/s) and the lowest median register (F#3) mean very full, bass-heavy, sustained chords.
sections.character: A firm, bass-heavy return of the swell, in which the dominant pushes forward and then falls warmly onto IV instead of home.
sections.dynamics: f, plateaued: intensity surges from 0.63 at 1:50 to 0.85 at 1:55, then holds between 0.70 and 0.79 until 2:15; the section average is -15.1 dBFS, the loudest section on average, though the single loudest moment remains 0:58.
sections.texture: Thick, sustained pedalled chords with a weighty bass line moving G–D–C, wide maj9/6/9 voicings and fewer separate attacks.
sections.register: Low-centred: bass C2–D2/G2, median F#3, top up to G5.
sections.emotional_beat: A reaffirmation: the feeling returns with greater certainty and weight, sustained rather than peaking and fading.
sections.imagery: A wide, slow ocean swell lifting under evening sun, broad and heavy, holding its height across the whole horizon.
sections.label: Second Swell (1:50-2:19)

sections.name: Ebbing Waters
sections.description: The swell recedes onto a long G (2:19, 2.5 s) shimmering between G and Gadd9 (2:21–2:24). The bass then moves off the tonic: Dmaj7 (labelled F#mb6b9/D at 2:25), D/A and D9/A (2:26–2:27), Am7 (2:27–2:29), Em11/D and Gmaj9/D (2:29). Gadd9 (2:31–2:33) and G9sus4/D (2:33) lead to a second ii–V circling over an A pedal: D/A, D9, Am7, C6/9#11/A, D7add6/A, D6/F# (2:34–2:37). It reaches Gmaj9/G/Gadd9 (2:38–2:41), with a final drift through D6 and D6/A (2:41–2:42), E7#5sus4/D (2:43) and Cmaj13#11/A (2:44). The A pedal and V-region emphasis explain the D-major local key estimate, but functionally this is ii–V–I in G with the dominant left suspended. Attacks are busiest here (2.88/s) while volume falls, giving a rippling, receding motion.
sections.character: Restless but quieting: the bass loosens from G and drifts over A, as if the music cannot quite settle.
sections.dynamics: mp falling to p: intensity 0.60 at 2:20, 0.44 at 2:25–2:30, 0.38 at 2:40; the section average is -22.4 dBFS.
sections.texture: Lighter, quicker rolling figures with a recurring A in the bass, open maj9/sus voicings above, and more frequent re-attacks at lower weight.
sections.register: Middle: bass around G2–A2, median B3, top touching B5; the timbre is dark and soft (centroid ~669 Hz).
sections.emotional_beat: Letting go: the warmth remains but the ground shifts, and a gentle uncertainty enters as the energy drains.
sections.imagery: Small ripples running across a lake after a large wave has passed, the light on the water breaking into scattered glints as dusk comes on.
sections.label: Ebbing Waters (2:19-2:45)

sections.name: Hovering Coda
sections.description: The coda begins in the piece's most shaded corner: Em9/F#, B5/F# and Bm/D (2:45–2:46), i.e. the iii chord over F# and D bass notes. A G major-7 voicing at 2:47 and Bm/D, D6 and D6add9 follow (2:49–2:50), with a chromatic passing 'Daug' (2:50), probably an A# passing tone. These resolve plagally onto C13/C6/C (2:51–2:54), Cadd9 over G and G/D, and a final long G (2:55–2:58, 3 s). One more brief shadow follows (Em11/D at 2:58; 'Gm69/D' at 2:59 is likely a transcription artefact) before IV returns as C6add9, Cadd9, C, C6 and Cmaj9 (2:59–3:02). The last bars dissolve: D/A/B and Gadd9 (3:03), C/G/A and Cmaj13/G (3:04–3:05), G6add9 (3:06), and finally a thin D5/A and an A–B–D cluster (3:07). The last sound is the 9th, 3rd and 5th of G with no firm root, an add9 suspension left ringing.
sections.character: A quiet, slightly bittersweet farewell that circles home through IV and ends hovering on an unresolved add9 rather than a closed cadence.
sections.dynamics: pp: intensity 0.34–0.35 at 2:45–2:50, a last small swell to 0.44 at 2:55 on the arrival of G, then fading to the quietest point at 3:04 (0.15 at 3:05); the section average is -27.6 dBFS.
sections.texture: Sparse: few attacks (1.74/s), thin rolled chords, Bm and iii shadows giving way to C and G, then a final cluster of upper chord tones without bass.
sections.register: Middle: bass from C2 rising away in the last seconds, median B3, top around C5, ending in a thin middle-register A–B–D.
sections.emotional_beat: Homecoming without a full stop: everything is at peace, but the last chord leaves the door gently open.
sections.imagery: The last pale light over a still field just after sunset, a faint mist rising, the horizon dissolving into lavender-grey.
sections.label: Hovering Coda (2:45-3:09)

tempo.description: The measured tactus is 58.7 BPM, roughly one beat per second, with an alternative level at 117.4 that captures the eighth-note rolling of the broken chords. Pulse clarity is low (0.38) but steadiness is high (0.89). The time is elastic: rubato breathes inside the phrase, yet the underlying pace stays very even. It feels slow and spacious for several reasons. Onsets come only about 2.2 times a second. Harmonic rhythm is broad: chords are held 1.5–3.5 s, and the tonic often sits for 8–10 beats (G 0:02–0:12). Deep bass re-strikes arrive about every 8 beats (0:04, 0:13, 0:21, 0:32), so the music moves in long eight-beat waves rather than bars. Local tempo barely shifts, from 56.4 BPM in the opening and 56.6 in the coda to 60.1 in Section 4. The ends relax slightly and the ebbing Section 4 moves fastest, with the highest attack rate (2.88/s) while getting quieter.

mode_balance.evidence:
Clearly major. Major chords take 81% of held duration and minor only 11%, giving a minor-weight of 0.05. No modal colour was detected by the measurement. The minor share comes almost entirely from diatonic ii and iii:
- Am7/Am9/Am11/Am13 at 0:49, 1:05–1:06, 1:15–1:17, 1:23–1:25, 2:27 and 2:35.
- Bm at 2:46–2:49 in the coda.
These shade the music rather than change its mode. The colours are 'bright-major' extensions: add9 and 6/9 on G and C, maj9/maj13 on both, and the raised 11th on C (C6/9#11, Cmaj13#11), which gives the IV chord a Lydian float without leaving the G-major collection. The frequent 'Bmb6M7/G' label is best read as a G major-7 voicing (G–B–D–F#, perhaps with A); it is a tonic colour, not a minor chord. True dominant-seventh sound is rare (2%) and appears mainly as D7 at 1:57 and 2:13–2:14. Even then it resolves to C, not G.

summary.overview: "Stand 10" is a flowing, densely arpeggiated E-minor meditation built almost entirely on one gesture: a floating upper structure (G–B–D–F#, the notes of Em9 and Gmaj7) suspended over a bass that rocks between E and C, later also D and A. The harmonic language is Aeolian with a constant Lydian glint on the VI chord (Cmaj9#11, CM6#11, C69#11 recur in every section). Pedal tones, sus2/sus4 colours (Esus24, Dsus24) and 9th/11th/13th labels dominate, so suspension wins over resolution throughout. Emotionally it is bittersweet and circling rather than tragic: it peaks early around 0:39, spends two minutes turning the same few chords over in different light, and finally lets go into a long decaying C chord and an unresolved E over D.
summary.key_center: E minor (Aeolian), measured with full clarity (1.0). The runner-up E major is a phantom created by the many 'E/G' and 'F#/E' labels, which are mostly Em with a G bass or overtone smear. The tonic is carried by an E pedal (E2/E3, median register E3), with VI (C) as the second pole. Brief tonicisations: VII (D6add9, Dsus24) and iv (Am9/C, A5/E) widen the loop in Section 1 (0:41, 0:52). The leading tone D# appears in Section 5 (B7#9/D at 2:33, E/D# at 2:40, E/G/D# at 2:47), giving a short harmonic-minor dominant pull. A C# colour at 3:02 (Em13/C#) and the F#/A sonority at 2:31 hint at E Dorian, but these are transient and possibly transcription artefacts. No real modulation occurs: every section's local key estimate is E minor. The ending (C/E held 3:39–3:49, then B/D and E/D at 3:49–3:50) closes on tonic colour without a clean V–i cadence.

mood.overall: A bittersweet, circling reverie in E minor: warm major-seventh light keeps falling across a minor ground, the energy crests early, and the piece gradually thins until it dissolves into a suspended, unresolved hush.

dynamics_arc.description: The overall shape is falling. The piece opens already at mf (0.64) and builds through Section 0 to a plateau in Section 1 (0.77–0.84, peak 0:40), holding strong through Section 2 (0.72–0.80). From about 1:45 it recedes in waves: 0.53 at 1:55, a breath back to 0.71 at 2:05, 0.51 at 2:25, a recovery around 0.63–0.68 through 2:35–3:00, and a final small swell to 0.74 at 3:05. Then comes a gradual decline to 0.55 at 3:30, followed by a sudden collapse to 0.29 at 3:35 and 0.16 at 3:40, leaving the coda's decaying chords. The 15.9 dB range is modest, so the drama lies in density and colour more than in loudness: transcribed notes fall from ~30/s in the first minute to ~17/s after 1:55.
dynamics_arc.climax_description: The climax arrives early, at about 0:39–0:41, inside Section 1. It is prepared by the loop widening from the bare i–VI rocking of Section 0 to a four-root bass walk (E–C–D–A) from 0:28. At the peak the harmony runs D7no5 / D13#9/C (0:38), Am69/C (0:39), FM7b5/E and Emadd4 (0:40), then D6add9 (0:41). It is a subtonic–subdominant swirl over the E pedal with no V–i cadence, so the high point feels like an opening of the chest rather than an arrival. A second, smaller push follows at 1:15 (0.80) and 1:35 (0.80) before the long recession.

summary.texture_and_register: The texture is a continuous pedal-sustained arpeggio ostinato throughout, with roughly 4 attacks/s from start to the coda. Transcribed note density, however, roughly halves after 1:55 (≈30 → ≈17 notes/s), so the second half sounds more transparent. The left hand anchors deep (G1 in Sections 0 and 3, C1 in Section 4) with an E pedal and roots on C, D and A. The right hand holds a near-static upper structure (G, B, D, F#, sometimes A and E) whose notes are shared by Em9, Gmaj7 and Cmaj9#11, so changes of bass recolour a nearly constant cloud. The median pitch never moves from E3 in any section, which is a striking sign of how centred and circular the writing is. The melodic peak, F#5, comes in Sections 2 and 4. Section 6 narrows the top to F#4 and brightens the tone through a lighter touch, and the coda reduces everything to a few chords around G2–F#4.
summary.emotional_narrative: The piece begins in motion (0:00–0:28): a rocking Em–Cmaj9#11 figure over an E pedal sets up a tender, unresolved question, rising steadily in intensity. From 0:28 the loop widens to take in D and A, and the music reaches its most open, ardent moment around 0:40, a crest built on suspended and added-tone chords rather than dominant arrival. At 0:57 the colour darkens: minor chords take an equal share, F#-over-E and D# clusters press against the tonic, and B-suspensions at 1:12–1:14 are left hanging. From 1:29 the music tries to rest in the warmth of C major, but the bass slides onto F# (1:51–1:54) and the ground shifts. After 1:55 the texture thins and the opening material returns as memory, quieter and more reflective, with augmented shadows (EmMaj7b6/C, Cdim7 at 2:26). At 2:31 small lights reappear: a B7#9 leading tone, D# inside the tonic, and a Dorian C# at 3:02 rekindle a cautious hope. From 3:04 the loop is played one last time with a lighter, brighter hand, distilled into the B–C semitone (Em#5). At 3:32 everything falls away to a long-ringing C chord and a final open E over D: the question is not answered, simply released.

imagery_cues.light: Diffuse, overcast light with intermittent warm breaks: brightest and widest around 0:40, clouding over from 0:57, flickering back as thin, cool glints after 2:30, and fading to a last violet glow in the final 20 seconds.
imagery_cues.motion: A continuous slow glide with a gentle side-to-side sway matching the half-bar E–C rocking (~1.2 s per swing). Drift forward steadily at walking pace, ease into longer, slower dissolves after 1:55, and come to a near standstill with a long held frame from 3:32.
imagery_cues.scale: Human-to-vast early: the loop widens into a broad open space at the 0:40 crest. Scale contracts after 1:55 to something closer and more intimate, and the coda shrinks to a single small point of light in a large dark space.
environments: a mist-covered lake at early morning
a forest clearing with light shafting through a high canopy
an open moorland under moving clouds
an empty high-ceilinged hall with a single pool of lamplight
a shoreline at dusk with water going glassy
imagery_cues.atmosphere: Cool, damp and still, with low cloud and light mist that thins and thickens; a faint breeze in the middle sections that dies to complete calm at the end.

chord_vocabulary: Cmaj7 / Cmaj9#11 / CM6#11 / C69#11 (VI with Lydian #11)
B7sus4 / Bsus4 / B7#9 (suspended or altered V)
summary.harmonic_highlights:
• 0:00–0:09: Em9 ↔ Cmaj9#11 over a shared G–B–D–F# upper structure. Only the bass moves (E ↔ C), which is the defining sound of the piece.
• 0:10: B7sus4, the first suspended dominant, left hanging rather than resolved.
• 0:21: D13/E, VII over the tonic pedal.
• 0:28–0:41: the loop widens to E–C–D–A, climaxing on D13#9/C → Am69/C → Emadd4 → D6add9 (0:38–0:41), with no V–i.
• 0:44: F#m7b5/C (iiø) into Em11/D → Dsus24.
• 0:56: Fmaj9#11, a fleeting flat-II/Phrygian shade (possibly passing or noise).
• 1:00: F#/E, F#-major colour over the E pedal.
• 1:12–1:14: Bsus4/B4 dominant suspension unresolved.
• 1:21: Dm13 F-natural shadow.
• 1:26–1:27: E–F#–D# cluster resolving into G6/Cadd9 at 1:28.
• 1:41–1:44: long-held C major, the VI as a false haven.
• 1:51–1:54: C chords over an F# bass, the tritone #11 made into the bass note and the most unstable point in the piece.
• 2:16 and 2:26: Emb6M7/C (C augmented colour) and Cdim7.
• 2:33: B7#9/D, the first true leading-tone dominant.
• 2:40 and 2:47: E/D# and E/G/D#, the major seventh inside the tonic.
• 3:02: Em13/C#, a Dorian sixth glint.
• 3:05–3:26: 'Em#5' = Em with B raised to C, the i–VI hinge distilled.
• 3:16: Bm7, minor v, avoiding dominant pull.
• 3:33–3:49: C major held ~15 s in decay, then B/D → E/D (3:49–3:50), an open ending on tonic-with-seventh.
summary.rhythm_and_feel: An even, rolling eighth-note arpeggio at ~99 BPM (the 197.8 level is the eighth-note grid) gives a constant flow of about 4 attacks per second. Pulse clarity is low (0.37) because the sustain pedal blurs downbeats and melodic leaps land inside the arpeggio rather than on strong beats. Steadiness, however, is high (0.86): this is elastic rubato around a stable centre, not free time. The harmonic rhythm is a half-bar rocking (≈1.2 s per bass change) for most of the piece, slowing to whole-bar or longer holds on C in Section 3 (1:41–1:44) and Section 4 (1:57). The tempo drifts slightly forward as the touch lightens (96 → 104 BPM from Section 0 to Section 6). The coda abandons pulse entirely for long held decays.
summary.relearning_tips:
1) Start with the core cell. Hold the right-hand upper structure G–B–D–F# (add E or A as passing tones) and rock the left hand between E2 (with B2) and C2 (with G2) every half-bar at ~96 BPM. This alone reproduces 0:00–0:28 and most of the piece. Notice that Em9 and Cmaj9#11 share every upper note, so keep the right hand nearly still and let the bass do the harmony.
2) Add the second layer of bass roots: D (D6add9, Dsus24) and A (A5/E, Am9/C). Practise the Section 1 walk E–C–D–A, and the climax bar around 0:38–0:41 (D13 → Am69/C → Esus/Em → D6add9), until the swell feels natural without a dominant.
3) Isolate the tension spots: the F#/E and D#/E/F# cluster at 1:26–1:27 resolving to G6/Cadd9, the F# bass under C at 1:51–1:54, and B7#9/D → A5/E at 2:33–2:34. Play them slowly and listen for how each one avoids a clean cadence.
4) Practise the B–C neighbour motion (Em → Em#5/C/E) in an inner voice; it is the heart of Section 6 and the hinge of the whole piece.
5) Then shape the dynamics. Peak around 0:40, recede in waves after 1:45, thin the voicings (fewer notes, not just softer) from 1:55, and lighten the touch for 3:04–3:32.
6) Finish by learning the coda as pure sound. Let C major ring for about 15 seconds before the B/D → E/D close, and resist resolving to a plain Em; the open E with D in the bass is the intended ending.
Note: labels such as Bb9sus (1:37), Fmaj9#11 (0:56) and the 'E/G' majors are likely transcription noise; check them against the recording before committing them to memory.
summary.title: Stand 10

sections.name: Rocking Pedal Opening
sections.description: The piece starts mid-motion with the core cell: an Em upper structure rocking against C. The sequence runs G/E 0:00, Cmaj#4 0:01, Em/G 0:02, Cmaj7/G 0:03, E5 0:04, Cmaj9#11/G 0:06, Esus24 0:07, Em9/G 0:08, Cmaj9#11/G 0:09. The upper notes G–B–D–F# barely move while the bass alternates E and C, so the chord change is felt mostly in the low register. Small widenings appear: B7sus4 at 0:10 (a suspended dominant that never resolves to a real B7), G6 at 0:12/0:15 and Gmaj13 at 0:17 (III colouring), D13/E at 0:21 (VII over the E pedal), and E7sus4 at 0:24. The section settles back onto Esus24 at 0:27. Melodic leaps are flagged roughly every 2–3 s (0:06, 0:09, 0:12, 0:17, 0:21…), suggesting a right-hand line that jumps between registers inside the arpeggio rather than moving stepwise.
sections.character: Restless but tender: a two-chord rocking that is lit from above by sustained ninths and sharp elevenths.
sections.dynamics: mf, building steadily from intensity 0.64 at 0:00 to 0.82 at 0:20–0:25
sections.texture: Dense rolling arpeggios over a sustained E/C bass pedal, with upper-structure ninths and #11s ringing in the sustain
sections.register: Wide: bass reaching G1 and E2, arpeggio centred around E3, melodic tops up to B4
sections.emotional_beat: Establishing the question: a looping, unresolved state that the rest of the piece will keep revisiting.
sections.imagery: Slow swells rolling under a pale sheet of mist on a dark lake, the surface lifting and settling in an even rhythm.
sections.label: Rocking Pedal Opening (0:00-0:28)

sections.name: Widening Loop Crest
sections.description: The loop opens outward. Next to Em and C, the bass now walks to D and A: C69#11/D 0:28, G6add9 0:30, C6 0:31, A5/E 0:32, Am9/C 0:33, A5/E 0:34, Am69/C 0:36. This adds iv and VII to the i–VI cell. The climax zone at 0:38–0:41 runs D7no5 / D13#9/C, Am69/C 0:39, Emadd4 0:40, then D6add9 0:41. It is a plagal–subtonic swirl that never takes the leading-tone path. F#m7b5/C (iiø) at 0:44 and Em11/D 0:44, followed by Dsus24 0:45, give the only pre-dominant tension. The passage then relaxes through Cmaj7 at 0:46–0:49 and repeated D6add9 at 0:52. It ends on Fmaj9#11 at 0:56, a fleeting flat-II/Phrygian shade (possibly a chromatic passing chord or noise) that tips into Section 2.
sections.character: The fullest, most open-hearted statement: the loop breathes wider and the sound reaches its loudest without ever becoming forceful.
sections.dynamics: Loudest section (-14 dBFS), f-leaning; peak intensity 0.84 at 0:40, easing to 0.76 by 0:55
sections.texture: Thick, pedal-sustained arpeggiation with bass movement on every half-bar and stacked 6/9 and 13th colours on top
sections.register: Bass C2–E2, core around E3, upper voice up to B4
sections.emotional_beat: The crest: the opening yearning swells into its widest, most hopeful reach.
sections.imagery: Morning light breaking through a canopy and spreading in widening rings across a forest floor.
sections.label: Widening Loop Crest (0:28-0:57)

sections.name: Shadowed Inner Turn
sections.description: The light dims. Brightness falls to ~1051 Hz and the minor share jumps to 41%, matching the major share. The section restarts on bare Em at 0:57, Em/G, Cmaj7 0:58, then an unusual F#/E at 1:00, which is F#-major colour over the E pedal (a Lydian II / V-of-V glint, partly ambiguous). Then Em, Cmaj7 / CM6#11 at 1:03, Am9/C 1:05, F#m7b5/C 1:06 (coinciding with the deep bass hit at 1:06), Em9/G and Em9/D 1:07. The second half runs Am9/G 1:11, Em11/B 1:11, Bsus4 1:12, B4 1:14: a suspended dominant again left hanging. Dm13 at 1:21 with FM7b9/C at 1:20 brings a brief F-natural shadow. The section closes with a cluster of E, F# and D# (F#/E 1:26, D#/E/F# 1:27). This is a tight leading-tone suspension around E that resolves softly into G6 and Cadd9 at 1:28. The melody touches its highest note here (F#5), above a darker, rounder accompaniment.
sections.character: Inward and clouded: the same loop now heard through minor-heavy harmony and a duskier tone.
sections.dynamics: Still strong (-13.9 dBFS) but less bright; intensity dips to 0.72 at 1:00 and 1:20 and rises back to 0.8 at 1:15
sections.texture: Dense arpeggios with a darker, lower-centroid colour; low bass impacts under clustered seconds (E–F#–D#)
sections.register: Bass C2–E2, median E3, melodic peak F#5
sections.emotional_beat: Doubt enters: the expansive feeling turns inward and questions itself, hanging on unresolved B-suspensions.
sections.imagery: Cloud shadow sliding across a hillside, the greens turning blue-grey while a single high glint remains on a distant ridge.
sections.label: Shadowed Inner Turn (0:57-1:29)

sections.name: Lingering on C
sections.description: The harmonic centre of gravity drifts to the VI chord. The sequence runs Cmaj#4 1:29, CM 1:30, Cmaj7 1:31–1:32, CM6#11 1:34, C69#11/G 1:35, CM6#11 1:37, Cmaj7/G 1:39, and CM held from 1:41 to about 1:44. Major chords account for 70% of held duration, so this passage feels brighter in harmony, even though the tone stays dark (~1063 Hz). Brief foreign tints include D9 / DMadd9 at 1:36 and a Bb9sus at 1:37, likely a passing chromatic sonority or transcription artefact. The ending is notable: from 1:51 to 1:54 the bass sits on F# under C chords (Esus2/F#, CM7b5/F#, F#/E). This makes the C–F# tritone, the #11, the actual bass note, and it is the most unstable moment in the piece. The attack rate is the highest so far (4.62/s), so the hands keep moving even as the intensity recedes to 0.63 by 1:50.
sections.character: A warm, hovering rest on the major sixth degree that ends by tilting onto an uneasy F# bass.
sections.dynamics: mf, receding: intensity ~0.8 at 1:35, falling to 0.63 at 1:50 and 0.53 at 1:55
sections.texture: Busy arpeggiation over long-held C sonorities; the bass reaches down to G1 and then shifts to F#
sections.register: Low-middle: bass G1–C2, core E3, upper line to A4
sections.emotional_beat: A false haven: the music tries to rest in the warmth of C but cannot settle, and the F# bass pulls the floor away.
sections.imagery: A pool of lamplight on the floor of a vast dim hall, its edge trembling as the air moves.
sections.label: Lingering on C (1:29-1:55)

sections.name: Thinning Reflection
sections.description: The texture thins noticeably (17.5 transcribed notes/s versus 26–31 earlier), and the music opens in near-stillness on Cmaj9/G, with Cmaj7/G held 1.5 s at 1:57. The core oscillation then returns more sparsely: E5 1:59, Em9/G 2:00, Gmaj13 / Esus24 2:01, Cmaj#4 2:02, Emadd9/G and Em 2:03, Em7 2:04. After that the loop settles into a three-chord rocking of E (Em/G, E/G), C (CM, E/C) and A5/E (iv over the E pedal) at 2:06–2:07, 2:12, 2:20 and 2:29. Chromatic colours over C include EmMaj7b6/C at 1:59 and Emb6M7/C at 2:16, which sound like C augmented / Cmaj7#5 (the B–C semitone with D#). A Cdim7 at 2:26 adds the darkest passing sonority. The bass dips as low as C1, giving occasional deep grounding under a lighter top. Intensity breathes from 0.53 at 1:55 up to 0.71 at 2:05, then sinks to 0.51 at 2:25.
sections.character: Pensive and quieter, like going back over the opening material with less weight in the hands.
sections.dynamics: mp, a gentle wave: 0.53 at 1:55 rising to 0.71 at 2:05, then falling to 0.51 at 2:25
sections.texture: Lighter, more open arpeggios with fewer simultaneous notes; occasional very low bass anchors
sections.register: Widest low reach (C1), core E3, top touching F#5
sections.emotional_beat: Withdrawal and remembering: the energy subsides and the opening idea returns as memory rather than statement.
sections.imagery: Dusk settling over flat water, ripples spreading farther apart as the wind drops.
sections.label: Thinning Reflection (1:55-2:30)

sections.name: Leading-Tone Glimmer
sections.description: The tone brightens (~1366 Hz) and the tempo nudges up to 100.3 BPM. The section opens on an ambiguous F#/A held around 2:31–2:33 (possibly F#m/A, a Dorian-tinged ii colour), then B7#9/D at 2:33.
