This is the first real dominant with the D# leading tone in the bass, though it moves to A5/E (2:34) and Esus4 (2:35) instead of a firm Em cadence. D# returns in E/D# at 2:40 and E/G/D# at 2:47, colouring the tonic with a major-seventh tension. The VII area is explored more fully here: D9/C 2:41, Em11/D and D6 2:42, D6add9 2:43, Em9/D 2:44, G6 2:46. A5/E recurs as a plagal pedal at 2:37, 2:48, 2:52 and 2:53–2:54 (with Asus4). The section closes with Esus2 3:00, Emadd9/G 3:01 and Em13/C# at 3:02, a C# Dorian sixth that adds a brief gleam.
sections.character: A quiet rekindling: leading tones and Dorian glints lift the colour without raising the volume.
sections.dynamics: mp to mf, steady around 0.63–0.68, nudging up to 0.68 at 3:00
sections.texture: Medium-density arpeggiation with long-held suspended sonorities (F#/A, A5/E) and a sustained E pedal
sections.register: Bass D2–E2, core E3, upper voice up to D5
sections.emotional_beat: Hope returns in small doses: the music finds new tensions (D#, C#) that point forward without committing.
sections.imagery: Thin shafts of late light through tall grass, flickering as the stems sway.
sections.label: Leading-Tone Glimmer (2:30-3:04)

sections.name: Brightening Recession
sections.description: This section has the brightest timbre of the full sections (~1575 Hz), the softest touch (mean velocity 44) and the quickest local tempo (103.9 BPM), so it feels lighter and more airborne. The 'Em#5' labels at 3:05, 3:07 and 3:26 are the defining voice-leading made audible. E–G–C is the Em triad with its fifth B lifted a semitone to C, the hinge that turns Em into C/E. In other words, the piece's i–VI motion is here distilled into a single B–C neighbour note. The harmony runs Em / Cmaj7/E 3:05, Am9/E 3:06, Cmaj9 3:08, Em11/D 3:11, C69#11 3:12, then a stepwise bass drift through Dsus24 / A7sus4 3:15, Bm7 3:16 (minor v, deliberately avoiding a dominant pull), DMadd9 3:16 and Dsus2 3:18. C6add9 is the most-held colour, appearing at 3:14, 3:19, 3:20 and 3:28, and alternates with A5/E and E/G. The section ends on Em9#5/C at 3:31, a C-rooted chord with E, G, B, D and F# stacked above: the full upper structure, about to be left ringing.
sections.character: Airy and receding, the familiar cell played with a lighter hand and a higher, clearer glow.
sections.dynamics: mp, a final small swell to 0.74 at 3:05, then receding to 0.55 at 3:30
sections.texture: Lighter-touch arpeggios with semitone neighbour motion (B–C) prominent in the upper voices; suspended chords on D and A
sections.register: Narrower: bass C2–E2, core E3, top no higher than F#4
sections.emotional_beat: Acceptance beginning: the loop is revisited one last time, more gently, as if already at a distance.
sections.imagery: Sunlight high in a pale sky glinting off slow-turning leaves as the branches thin out.
sections.label: Brightening Recession (3:04-3:32)

sections.name: Dissolving Coda
sections.description: The music suddenly drops to near silence (-51 dBFS, intensity 0.16 at 3:40) and the attack rate falls to 1.27/s. A few final placements set up the ending (E/G/A and G/E at 3:32, C6/G at 3:33), then a C major chord over G is held for about 5 s (3:33–3:38). It is re-struck or re-voiced as CM and C/E at 3:39 and left to decay for roughly 10 s until 3:49. At 3:49–3:50 come B/D and E/D. These read best as a soft dominant touch (B with D, effectively Bm or B with a lowered third) followed by E over D: a tonic with its seventh in the bass, unresolved. The 100% 'major' share comes from only a handful of long, quiet chords; the high brightness (~2397 Hz) reflects decay, overtones and room tone rather than real brilliance. The piece closes with the open ear typical of Barnoski: suspended, not cadenced.
sections.character: A held breath that evaporates: VI lingering in the air, then a quiet, open-ended E.
sections.dynamics: ppp, a sudden drop at 3:32, quietest at 3:42, with a faint re-touch rising to 0.23 by 3:50
sections.texture: Sparse sustained chords decaying in the pedal; almost no new attacks
sections.register: Middle: G2–F#4, centred around E3
sections.emotional_beat: Release without answer: the circling stops and the question is left hanging in the air.
sections.imagery: The last ring of a ripple fading on perfectly still water at dusk, a faint glow over a dark shoreline.
sections.label: Dissolving Coda (3:32-3:54)

tempo.description: The measured tactus of 98.9 BPM sits at a moderate walking speed, but the piece feels 'flowing' rather than walking. About 4.1 attacks per second of rolling arpeggiation fill every beat, and the alternative 197.8 level shows the eighth-note motion is almost as salient as the beat. Pulse clarity is low (0.37) while steadiness is high (0.86): the time is even, but the downbeats are softened by pedal wash and elastic rubato, so it floats more than it marches. Harmonic rhythm is the key to the felt speed. The bass changes roughly every half-bar (~1.2 s: Em at 0:02, Cmaj7/G at 0:03, E5 at 0:04, Cmaj9#11/G at 0:06, Esus24 at 0:07), producing a gentle rocking. Local tempo drifts upward late in the piece (100.3 BPM in Section 5, 103.9 in Section 6) as the playing gets lighter. In the coda (118 BPM nominal, only 1.27 attacks/s) the pulse effectively dissolves.

mode_balance.evidence: By duration, major chords account for 57% and minor for only 21%. That does not make the piece major. The 'major' share is dominated by C-family chords (Cmaj7, Cmaj9#11, CM6#11, C69#11), which are the VI of E minor, plus G6/Gmaj13 (III) and D6add9 (VII). All three are diatonic Aeolian chords. The tonal centre that the pedal, the section key estimates and the Krumhansl profile all point to is E, and E itself is almost always minor or open: Em9, Emadd9, Em7add11, E5, Esus24. Hence the measured minor-weight of 0.71 and the minor-dominant verdict. The #11 on C (F#) is simply scale degree 2 of E minor, so the 'Lydian' sheen is native to the key rather than borrowed. The suspended share (8%; 13% in Section 0) keeps thirds ambiguous, which explains why the minor sounds wistful rather than dark. Possible chromatic colours include D# leading tone (2:33–2:47), C# Dorian sixth (3:02), and F natural in Fmaj9#11 at 0:56 and Dm13 at 1:21, a fleeting Phrygian shadow. Each is brief and should be treated as colour or possible noise rather than a modal shift.
